missions.title: The one-room escape game
missions.description: Design a tiny escape-room puzzle for your partner using three linked clues.
steps: Choose a final harmless object as the treasure and make a clue pointing to it.
Work backwards to create two earlier clues, using wordplay, a sketch, or a simple code.
Let your partner solve the three clues, then trade designer and detective roles.
missions.finish: Each of you has solved the other's three-clue trail.
missions.apart: Send clues one at a time and use photos of objects instead of hidden locations.

missions.title: The three-stop treasure trail
missions.description: Build a tiny local trail with a view, a discovery, and a good place to pause.
steps: Choose three nearby public places: one interesting detail, one pleasant view, and one place to sit.
Visit them in the order your partner chooses; each person leads one stop.
Give the trail a name and write a one-line clue for each stop.
missions.finish: You have walked your three-stop trail and kept its clues.

missions.title: The pantry plot twist
missions.description: Make a small dish from four ingredients you already have, with one surprising presentation.
missions.supplies: Four agreed ingredients and your usual kitchen tools
steps: Agree on four familiar ingredients that fit both of your food needs.
Each suggest a dish; combine your ideas into one snack or meal.
Plate it as if it belongs to an imaginary restaurant and write a one-line menu description.
missions.finish: You have made, tasted, and named your four-ingredient dish.
missions.apart: Use overlapping ingredients in your kitchens and compare the results on a call.

missions.title: The parallel treasure hunt
missions.description: Send your partner five clues to treasures they can find in their own surroundings.
steps: Each write five clues about types of things, such as a perfect circle or something that looks like a face.
Exchange the clues and find a photo, sketch, or written answer for each without buying anything.
Reveal the ten finds and choose the most surprising match.
missions.finish: Both five-clue collections are complete.

missions.title: The five-shot movie
missions.description: Film a tiny story with a beginning, a twist, and an ending.
steps: Pick a harmless plot: a missing snack, a heroic sock, or a jealous mug.
Record exactly five short shots; use objects as the cast if you prefer.
Watch the shots in order and give your film a title.
missions.finish: Your five shots tell one complete story.
missions.apart: Each film two shots, then make the fifth together on a call.

missions.title: The paper-plane airshow
missions.supplies: Scrap paper and a clear floor space
missions.description: Build two paper planes for a friendly landing contest.
steps: Each choose and fold a different paper-plane design.
Mark three low floor landing zones with paper.
Take five gentle flights each and improve one fold.
missions.finish: Your two designs have completed a scored five-flight test.

missions.title: The sock-volley living room league
missions.supplies: A soft rolled sock and a clear space
missions.description: Keep a soft sock ball airborne in a cooperative mini game.
steps: Choose a clear comfortable area and agree seated or standing play.
Count gentle alternating touches before the sock lands.
Try three rounds and beat your first shared score.
missions.finish: Your team has completed three scored rally attempts.

missions.title: The market ingredient relay
missions.description: Choose one new-to-you ingredient and turn it into a shared snack.
steps: Agree a budget and ingredients that suit both of you.
Choose one unfamiliar food from a local shop or market.
Prepare it by a reliable simple method and review it together.
missions.finish: Your ingredient discovery has become a finished tasted snack.

missions.title: The forced-perspective giant
missions.supplies: A camera and a small object
missions.description: Make a tiny object look enormous using perspective.
steps: Choose a safe stationary scene with good light.
Place the object near the camera and your partner farther away.
Adjust until the scales create a convincing visual joke.
missions.finish: Your photo makes the tiny object look gigantic.

missions.title: The encyclopedia link race
missions.description: Travel between two unrelated topics using article links.
steps: Agree a start page and a reasonable destination.
Follow only links inside articles without using search.
Compare your routes and keep the most surprising connection.
missions.finish: Both routes reach the destination or reveal a shared new topic.
missions.apart: Start together and compare routes on a call.

missions.title: The homemade pizza face-off
missions.supplies: Ingredients for a familiar simple pizza method
missions.description: Make two personal pizzas with different flavor plans.
steps: Choose a reliable method and suitable ingredients together.
Each assemble a small pizza with a clear flavor theme.
Cook as directed and share a tasting of both.
missions.finish: Your two personal pizzas have been cooked and compared.

missions.title: The beginner juggling club
missions.description: Try a beginner juggling progression together.
steps: Find a clear free beginner demonstration using soft objects.
Practice one toss, then two, before attempting three.
Compare one small improvement and finish with your best attempt.
missions.finish: Both people have tried the three practice stages.
missions.apart: Practice separately and show progress on a call.

missions.title: The object heist
missions.description: Recover a mystery object using only five clues from your partner.
steps: Each secretly choose an object you can see.
Take turns giving five clues without saying its name; the other guesses or points to it.
Swap roles and invent an unnecessarily dramatic codename for each object.
missions.finish: You have solved both mystery objects.
missions.apart: On a call, show each recovered object to the camera.

missions.title: Tabletop mini-golf
missions.description: Build three paper-ball golf holes and play a homemade championship.
missions.supplies: Scrap paper, a spoon, and three containers
steps: Set three targets on a clear table or floor and make a small paper ball.
Take turns nudging the ball with a spoon; give each hole one playful obstacle.
Play all three holes, count attempts, and name the hardest hole.
missions.finish: Both of you have completed your three-hole course.

missions.title: The twelve-minute skill trade
missions.description: Trade a small skill you can actually teach and leave with two new abilities.
missions.supplies: Whatever you already use for your chosen skills
steps: Each choose one skill you can demonstrate, such as a phone shortcut, paper fold, or drawing trick.
Give each other a twelve-minute lesson with a chance to practice.
Have the learner demonstrate it back and choose where they might use it.
missions.finish: Each of you can demonstrate one new skill without prompts.
missions.apart: Teach over a call and choose skills using materials you both have.

missions.title: The zero-cost care package
missions.description: Assemble a small care package for someone using things you already have.
missions.supplies: Paper and a few suitable items already at home
steps: Choose someone you know would welcome a small gesture and agree what might brighten their day.
Make a package with one useful thing, one amusing thing, and a handwritten note.
Decide how to offer it with no pressure to accept, then deliver or arrange it yourselves.
missions.finish: Your three-part care package is ready and has been offered.

missions.title: The ordinary-day time capsule
missions.description: Preserve a normal day in five small details your future selves might forget.
steps: Each collect a current sound, a small photo or sketch, and one exact phrase from the day.
Choose five pieces between you and add the date plus a short note explaining each one.
Pick a date to revisit the capsule and keep it somewhere both of you can find.
missions.finish: Your dated five-piece capsule has a revisit date and a home.
missions.apart: Combine details from your two places into one capsule.

missions.title: The sign sentence scramble
missions.description: Build a ridiculous sentence using words from public signs.
steps: Collect eight words along a short public route.
Use each word once in a single sentence.
Read your sentence as a dramatic announcement.
missions.finish: Your eight found words form one complete sentence.
missions.apart: Collect four words each and combine them on a call.

missions.title: The missing-scene prediction
missions.supplies: A legally free short film both can access
missions.description: Predict a story's next move using visible clues rather than guessing wildly.
steps: Choose a free short film and agree one pause before the final section.
Each note a prediction and two clues from what you have seen.
Finish the film and compare which clues were useful or misleading.
missions.finish: Both predictions have been checked against the completed story.
missions.apart: Pause your own copies at the same agreed point on a call.

missions.title: The popcorn seasoning panel
missions.description: Compare three tiny popcorn seasoning blends.
steps: Choose seasonings that suit both people's dietary needs.
Make small labeled samples with different familiar blends.
Taste and choose a house favorite.
missions.finish: Your popcorn lab has a chosen signature blend.

missions.title: The leaf silhouette atlas
missions.description: Draw five leaf shapes without picking anything.
steps: Observe leaves on an accessible public path or your own plants.
Sketch five visibly different silhouettes.
Give each a descriptive nickname before checking any identification.
missions.finish: Your sketchbook contains five distinct observed leaf shapes.
missions.apart: Compare leaf atlases from your separate locations.

missions.title: The blanket-fort reading room
missions.description: Build a comfortable low blanket fort for a tiny reading café.
steps: Drape blankets securely without covering heaters or lights.
Each choose a short passage to read aloud.
Spend ten minutes enjoying your finished reading room.
missions.finish: Your fort has hosted two short readings.

missions.title: The library cover lottery
missions.description: Pick reading discoveries using three playful cover clues.
steps: Check your library's opening and access information.
Find covers featuring a doorway, a creature, and one chosen color.
Each read a blurb and recommend one discovery.
missions.finish: Your library hunt has three finds and two recommendations.

missions.title: The kitchen rhythm quartet
missions.description: Build a gentle four-part rhythm from ordinary objects.
steps: Choose four objects that make quiet distinct sounds.
Each create a short repeating two-object rhythm.
Combine the parts and perform a thirty-second piece.
missions.finish: Your four-object rhythm has a complete shared performance.

missions.title: The paper tower trade
missions.description: Build two paper towers then trade one design improvement.
steps: Each build a freestanding tower using three sheets.
Compare what keeps each design upright.
Swap one construction tip and rebuild once.
missions.finish: Both paper towers have completed an improved second attempt.

missions.title: The mystery envelope afternoon
missions.description: Let three playful envelopes decide your next tiny adventure.
steps: Write one indoor, one outdoor, and one creative activity you can do.
Choose among the feasible envelopes at random.
Do the selected activity and draw its souvenir badge.
missions.finish: Your chosen envelope has become a completed little adventure.

missions.title: The color expedition
missions.description: Find a five-color palette hiding in a familiar street or park.
steps: Each choose two colors; pick a fifth color together.
Find each color on a familiar public route without moving or taking anything.
Arrange five photos or sketches into a palette and name the place it represents.
missions.finish: Your five-color local palette is complete.
missions.apart: Collect colors in your own neighborhoods, then combine your favorites.

missions.title: The stop-motion snack
missions.description: Make an everyday object appear to move by itself in a short stop-motion film.
missions.supplies: Phone camera and a small object
steps: Choose a character and a simple destination, such as a sock reaching its pair.
Take twelve photos, moving the character a little between shots and keeping the camera still.
Swipe through the images quickly or use a tool you already have to animate them.
missions.finish: Your twelve-frame story shows the character reaching its destination.
missions.apart: Each make six frames of the character's journey and exchange them.

missions.title: The three-word ban
missions.description: Help your partner guess an object while avoiding its three most obvious clues.
steps: Each write five everyday objects and three forbidden clue words for each.
Swap lists; describe each object for up to thirty seconds without using its name or banned words.
Play both sets and choose the most ridiculous successful clue.
missions.finish: You have played ten clues and recorded your funniest one.
missions.apart: Read the lists and play over a call or exchange voice notes.

missions.title: The toast tournament
missions.description: Invent three tiny toast toppings and give them a proper championship.
missions.supplies: Bread or crackers and toppings you already have
steps: Choose three topping combinations together, including one you have never tried.
Make small portions and give each combination a name.
Taste, score flavor and surprise, and write the winning combination as a recipe.
missions.finish: Your tasting has a winner and a repeatable recipe.
missions.apart: Make the same three combinations where possible or compare local substitutes.

missions.title: Local history detectives
missions.description: Solve one small question about a place you pass all the time.
missions.supplies: A public sign, library source, or reliable local archive
steps: Choose a question about a nearby street name, building, landmark, or public artwork.
Each find one source and compare what it actually supports.
Write a three-sentence story with your sources and one detail still worth investigating.
missions.finish: You have a sourced answer to your local question.
missions.apart: Research a place from each neighborhood and exchange your findings.

missions.title: The useful little map
missions.description: Make a genuinely useful local map that your future selves or a friend could use.
steps: Pick a practical theme, such as public water fountains, free places to sit, or free local exhibits.
Find three public options and check their access information rather than guessing.
Make a three-stop map with one useful note for each place and who it would help.
missions.finish: Your checked three-stop map is ready to use or share.
missions.apart: Contribute locations from both areas and make two mini maps.

missions.title: The six-song chapter
missions.description: Build a six-song soundtrack for the current chapter of your lives.
missions.supplies: Music you can already access and a notes app
steps: Each choose a song for this week's mood, a recent memory, and something you are looking forward to.
Take turns playing excerpts or naming the songs and explaining your three choices.
Put all six in order and give the chapter a title plus a one-line cover note.
missions.finish: Your six-song chapter has an order, a title, and a cover note.
missions.apart: Listen together on a call or exchange short explanations alongside the song names.

missions.title: The two-city gallery
missions.description: Open one tiny exhibition with artwork made in two different places.
missions.supplies: Paper or a drawing tool and a call
steps: Agree on one theme and each make two small pieces using materials already nearby.
Give each piece a title and a one-sentence artist's note.
Hold a gallery-opening call and take turns introducing the other person's work.
missions.finish: Your four-piece exhibition has a title and has had its opening.

missions.title: The shape bingo block
missions.description: Play bingo with shapes hiding in public details.
steps: Draw a grid with nine different simple shapes.
Walk a familiar route looking for matching details.
Mark five finds and sketch the most surprising match.
missions.finish: Your shape card has five checked discoveries.
missions.apart: Compare separate bingo cards after your walks.

missions.title: The monochrome scavenger roll
missions.description: Build a five-photo collection dominated by one color.
steps: Each choose a color for the other.
Find five scenes that strongly feature your assigned color.
Arrange the photos as one miniature exhibition.
missions.finish: Your color collection contains five distinct subjects.
missions.apart: Exchange your completed color galleries.

missions.title: The one-object blockbuster
missions.description: Make a short trailer starring a household object.
steps: Give the object a goal and an enemy.
Record three short shots with dramatic narration.
Play the trailer with an original film title.
missions.finish: Your object has a complete three-shot trailer.
missions.apart: Exchange trailers and invent review quotes for each other.

missions.title: The fruit ripeness blind labels
missions.supplies: Two suitable pieces of the same fruit
missions.description: Compare how ripeness changes the same fruit rather than judging its appearance.
steps: Choose two safe-to-eat examples at different suitable ripeness levels.
Prepare labeled small portions without hiding any ingredients.
Taste and compare sweetness, texture, and the best use for each.
missions.finish: Both samples have a compared flavor profile and a specific suggested use.

missions.title: The cloud comic strip
missions.description: Turn changing clouds into a three-panel fictional story.
steps: Choose a comfortable safe place to observe the sky.
Sketch three shapes that suggest characters or objects.
Link the sketches with a tiny invented plot.
missions.finish: Your sky observations form a complete three-panel comic.
missions.apart: Combine cloud characters seen from different places.

missions.title: The floor-picnic cinema club
missions.supplies: A blanket, snacks, and a free short film
missions.description: Host a miniature indoor picnic premiere.
steps: Arrange a comfortable blanket picnic with familiar snacks.
Choose a legally free short film you can both access.
Watch it and invent a fictional festival prize.
missions.finish: Your indoor picnic screening has a chosen award winner.

missions.title: The bakery texture scout
missions.supplies: A public display and your own notebook
missions.description: Learn what visual clues suggest a baked food's texture before reading its description.
steps: From a public display choose three items without blocking access.
Each predict texture using visible clues such as layers or crust.
Check public labels for preparation clues and record which predictions remain uncertain.
missions.finish: Your three texture predictions are separated into checked clues and untested guesses.

missions.title: The five-second intro wager
missions.description: Guess familiar songs from short introductions while testing how confident you should be.
steps: Each choose three accessible tracks the other might recognize.
Play only the first few seconds from your own accessible copy.
Give a title guess and confidence score before the reveal.
missions.finish: Six intro guesses have been checked with their original confidence scores.
missions.apart: Take turns controlling playback during a call.

missions.title: The cardboard marble-free maze
missions.supplies: Cardboard, tape, and a paper ball
missions.description: Build a tilt maze for a light paper ball.
steps: Draw a short route inside a shallow scrap box.
Add low cardboard walls with tape.
Tilt gently until the ball reaches the finish.
missions.finish: Your homemade maze has one completed successful run.

missions.title: The free-museum treasure list
missions.description: Find five oddly specific details in a public online collection.
steps: Choose a collection viewable without payment or an account.
Look for a blue hat, animal, window, food, and unusual shoe.
Share the five artwork links and your favorite detail.
missions.finish: Your online museum hunt has five checked discoveries.
missions.apart: Split the hunt or compare separate finds remotely.

missions.title: The one-color outfit outing
missions.description: Dress around one randomly chosen color for a tiny outing.
steps: Write six available clothing colors and draw one.
Build comfortable outfits around the chosen color.
Take a short familiar walk and find three matching details.
missions.finish: Your color-themed outing has three matching discoveries.

missions.title: Receipt poetry duel
missions.description: Turn ordinary words into a poem you would actually keep.
steps: Choose a text with at least twenty words.
Each borrow exactly eight words from it to make a tiny poem.
Read both poems with full dramatic commitment and pick a line to keep.
missions.finish: You have two eight-word poems and a favorite line.
missions.apart: Use a photo of the same text so you share the word bank.

missions.title: The miniature landmark tour
missions.description: Discover the details everyone walks past and turn them into a tiny sightseeing guide.
steps: Walk a familiar public route and look for three small details: a sign, a pattern, and a tiny piece of history.
Take turns being a tour guide; give each detail a memorable title.
Make a three-entry guide with one photo or sketch and one sentence per stop.
missions.finish: You have made a guide to three overlooked landmarks.
missions.apart: Each contribute details from your own neighborhood and give a virtual tour.

missions.title: The cardboard arcade
missions.description: Build a playable tabletop game from packaging you would otherwise recycle.
missions.supplies: Clean packaging, paper, and tape if available
steps: Pick a game goal: land a paper ball, balance a piece, or guide a token through a course.
Build one playable round using only materials you already have.
Give the game a name and each play three attempts; adjust one rule together.
missions.finish: Your homemade game works and both of you have played it.

missions.title: The coin bridge
missions.description: Build a paper bridge that holds a coin, then improve it together.
missions.supplies: Three scrap sheets, two books, and a coin
steps: Place two books about a hand-width apart and design a bridge using only your paper.
Test whether it can hold one coin for ten seconds; notice where it bends.
Redesign it together and test the improved version.
missions.finish: Your second design holds the coin or teaches you exactly what to change next.
missions.apart: Build separate prototypes and trade one improvement before the final tests.

missions.title: The pop-up restaurant
missions.description: Open a one-table restaurant using an ordinary meal and a wildly specific theme.
missions.supplies: A meal, paper, and whatever is already at home
steps: Pick a theme such as a moon diner, a train café, or a tiny seaside hotel.
Make a short menu and change one detail of the table to match it.
Serve your ordinary meal in character and write a two-sentence restaurant review together.
missions.finish: Your restaurant has served one meal and received its first review.

missions.title: One bird, one tree
missions.description: Learn to recognize two living neighbors and make a small field guide.
missions.supplies: Notes or a camera; a field guide if available
steps: In a familiar public outdoor spot, choose one bird and one tree or plant to observe without disturbing them.
Sketch or describe two distinguishing features of each, then check a reliable identification guide.
Compare your guesses and write how you would recognize them next time.
missions.finish: You have two field-guide entries with features and a checked identification or an honest unknown.
missions.apart: Observe your own areas and introduce your finds on a call.

missions.title: The appreciation dispatch
missions.description: Give two people a specific thank-you they would not hear in an ordinary week.
missions.supplies: Paper or your usual messaging method
steps: Each choose a person whose quiet effort you have noticed.
Write a short note naming the effort, its effect, and one thing you genuinely value.
Offer the notes yourselves, then tell each other what made those people come to mind.
missions.finish: Both specific thank-yous have been offered, with no reply required.
missions.apart: Write and send your own notes, then catch up on a call.

missions.title: The two-camera story
missions.description: Tell the same small outing from two different points of view.
missions.supplies: Two cameras or one camera you take turns using
steps: Choose a short outing and take exactly three photos each without directing the other person.
Reveal the photos afterwards and notice what each of you paid attention to.
Choose four images to tell the outing as a beginning, two middle moments, and an ending.
missions.finish: Your four-image story includes both perspectives.

missions.title: The map-room expedition
missions.description: Explore an unfamiliar city online by guiding each other between three public landmarks.
missions.supplies: An online map or a library's public map collection
steps: Choose a city neither of you knows well and each research one public landmark.
Take turns guiding the other through three map stops, adding one reliable fact or honest observation at each.
Make a tiny route card and pick the stop you would most like to see for real.
missions.finish: You have a three-stop route and a shared favorite.

missions.title: The color memory decoy
missions.description: Test how accurately you remember a scene's colors after walking away.
steps: Observe one safe public scene for thirty seconds without photographing it.
Step aside and independently list five colors and their locations.
Return and check which details your memory invented or missed.
missions.finish: Both five-detail color memories have been checked against the scene.
missions.apart: Use the same public image, hide it, then reveal it for checking.

missions.title: The shadow creature portrait
missions.description: Photograph a new creature made entirely from shadows.
steps: Arrange your hands or ordinary objects near a wall.
Adjust a cool lamp to create an unexpected silhouette.
Capture the creature and name its species.
missions.finish: Your shadow creature has a clear portrait and name.
missions.apart: Reveal your creature portraits on a call.

missions.title: The homemade nature documentary
missions.description: Film a wildlife documentary about imaginary indoor creatures.
steps: Choose three objects as your documentary's subjects.
Record close shots with a gentle narrator voice.
End with one surprising fictional creature fact.
missions.finish: Your indoor documentary introduces three imaginary species.
missions.apart: Send separate documentary segments and watch together.

missions.title: The crunchy-soft contrast
missions.description: Build a bite that balances crunch and softness.
steps: Choose two foods you already enjoy safely.
Try three different proportions in tiny portions.
Compare texture balance before picking your favorite.
missions.finish: Your snack has a tested preferred crunch-to-soft ratio.

missions.title: The bird-call listener log
missions.supplies: Paper and a reliable bird guide
missions.description: Compare three bird-like sounds without approaching wildlife.
steps: Listen quietly from an ordinary accessible spot.
Describe three sounds using your own funny syllables.
Check a trusted guide for possible matches without claiming certainty.
missions.finish: Your listening log includes three described sound patterns.
missions.apart: Exchange your written sound descriptions after listening.

missions.title: The rainy-window bingo
missions.description: Play a gentle observation game from your own window.
steps: Draw a grid of nine ordinary things you might see.
Observe from indoors without tracking individual people.
Mark five finds and sketch the most surprising one.
missions.finish: Your window bingo has five observed squares.
missions.apart: Compare bingo cards from your different window views.

missions.title: The one-snack local tour
missions.description: Make one small snack purchase the centerpiece of a local outing.
steps: Agree a budget and check ingredients together.
Choose one snack and a nearby public place to pause.
Share it and write a one-line tour review.
missions.finish: Your tiny snack tour has a stop and joint review.

missions.title: The dance move trading cards
missions.supplies: Paper and a comfortable clear space
missions.description: Invent three gentle dance moves and illustrate them as cards.
steps: Choose moves you can comfortably do seated or standing.
Draw an instruction card for each original move.
Shuffle the cards and perform their order.
missions.finish: Your three-move routine has been performed from shuffled cards.
missions.apart: Reveal your cards and dance together on video.

missions.title: The one-sheet paper chair
missions.description: Design a tiny paper chair that stands by itself.
steps: Fold one sheet without adding extra supports.
Test whether a small paper character can sit on it.
Adjust one fold and compare the improved chair.
missions.finish: Your paper chair supports its paper guest.
missions.apart: Exchange chair photos and trade one improvement tip.

missions.title: The map-label memory challenge
missions.description: Reconstruct a small real map after its labels are hidden.
steps: Choose a public park or landmark district with five useful labels.
Study the map for one minute, then sketch the layout without looking.
Reveal the map and correct locations before comparing your memory strategies.
missions.finish: Both five-label map sketches have been checked against the original.
missions.apart: Use the same public map and reveal your sketches together.

missions.title: The one-song dance
missions.description: Invent a short dance together, including one move that makes you laugh.
steps: Pick a song you both want to hear.
Each invent two comfortable movements; seated movements count.
Put all four moves together and perform them once through the chorus.
missions.finish: You have performed your four-move dance together.
missions.apart: Mirror each other over a call; recording is optional.

missions.title: The bench council
missions.description: Find your local headquarters by testing three places to sit and watch the world.
steps: Choose three nearby public seats or spots where sitting is allowed.
Spend three minutes at each; score comfort, view, and people-watching without photographing strangers.
Pick your headquarters and decide one small occasion to return for.
missions.finish: Your three-stop scorecard has a winning headquarters.

missions.title: The shadow stage
missions.description: Put on a one-minute shadow play with a plot twist chosen by your partner.
missions.supplies: A lamp and paper or household objects
steps: Each choose one character you can make as a shadow.
One person starts a simple story; the other adds an unexpected twist halfway through.
Perform a one-minute version and give your production a title.
missions.finish: You have performed one complete shadow story.
missions.apart: Take turns presenting your stage over a call.

missions.title: The emergency radio show
missions.description: Broadcast three minutes of fictional news using three ordinary objects as your headlines.
missions.supplies: Three objects and an optional recorder
steps: Each choose an ordinary object; select a third together.
Turn the objects into three fictional news stories and split anchor, reporter, and guest roles.
Perform a three-minute broadcast with a serious opening and a deeply unserious weather report.
missions.finish: Your show has three stories and a sign-off.
missions.apart: Record alternating segments or perform together on a call.

missions.title: The snack-swap studio
missions.description: Recreate each other's ideal snack using the ingredients already in your kitchens.
steps: Each describe a snack using three qualities, such as crunchy, warm, and tangy.
Design a small snack meeting the other person's brief without buying anything.
Taste or present the results and give each snack a name.
missions.finish: You have made two snacks matching your three-word briefs.
missions.apart: Show your snacks over a call and compare what the same brief produced.

missions.title: The repair rookies
missions.description: Learn one small repair together and give an everyday object a second chance.
missions.supplies: A low-risk item and repair supplies you already have
steps: Choose a small repair such as a loose button, a torn paper cover, or a simple fabric patch.
Find instructions and practice the technique on scrap material first.
Complete the repair together and take a before-and-after note or photo.
missions.finish: One small item is repaired or you know exactly which part needs outside help.

missions.title: A book's next chapter
missions.description: Give a book you are finished with a thoughtful next destination.
missions.supplies: A book you own and are ready to pass on
steps: Each choose a book you can give away and write a short, spoiler-free recommendation.
Find a willing reader or a book-exchange shelf that accepts donations; check before leaving anything.
Pass the book on with the recommendation and tell your partner why you chose it.
missions.finish: Your chosen books have an agreed next home or a checked handoff plan.
missions.apart: Find readers or exchanges in your own areas and compare your recommendations.

missions.title: Voice postcards
missions.description: Record a short voice message that captures a place and a moment, not just an update.
missions.supplies: Phone recorder or Little Us voice notes
steps: Choose a place where you can comfortably record without capturing private conversations.
Each record one minute: describe three details, one sound, and one reason you chose that place.
Listen to both postcards and give each one a title and a date.
missions.finish: Two titled, dated voice postcards are kept.
missions.apart: Record from your separate places and exchange them when you both have time to listen.

missions.title: The pocket parcel
missions.description: Make a five-piece digital parcel that feels like it came from your corner of the world.
missions.supplies: Photos, notes, or voice recordings you can share
steps: Each collect a view, a small sound, a local detail, a doodle, and a short personal message.
Arrange the five pieces in an order that tells a little story.
Exchange parcels and name the detail that made the other place feel most vivid.
missions.finish: Both five-piece parcels have been sent and opened.

missions.title: The sidewalk movie scout
missions.description: Find locations for three scenes in an imaginary film.
steps: Choose scenes for an arrival, a chase, and a finale.
Find public views that could suggest each scene.
Sketch a three-shot storyboard without filming other people.
missions.finish: Your film has three scouted scene settings.
missions.apart: Trade scouting photos from your separate neighborhoods.

missions.title: The household album still
missions.description: Stage a cinematic album image using three household props.
steps: Choose a musical mood without copying an existing cover.
Arrange three props in available light.
Photograph and add an original album title.
missions.finish: Your three-prop scene has become an original album cover.
missions.apart: Swap cover images and invent each other's first track.

missions.title: The dubbed household scene
missions.description: Give a silent everyday scene an entirely different story.
steps: Record a harmless thirty-second scene with no dialogue.
Watch it once and invent an unrelated storyline.
Perform new voices and sound effects while it plays.
missions.finish: Your silent clip has a completed alternative soundtrack.

missions.title: The familiar-flavor soda shop
missions.description: Create a tiny café drink from ingredients you already use.
steps: Choose a normal drink base and two familiar additions.
Mix small samples using different proportions.
Name the favorite and write its exact recipe.
missions.finish: Your imaginary café has a repeatable signature drink.
missions.apart: Prepare separate drinks and exchange recipe cards.

missions.title: The moss-world drawing
missions.description: Imagine a whole world inside a small patch of greenery.
steps: Observe a mossy or grassy patch without touching it.
Sketch it as a landscape for tiny fictional explorers.
Add three imaginary landmarks on your drawing.
missions.finish: Your small green patch has a three-landmark fantasy map.
missions.apart: Trade your tiny landscape drawings remotely.

missions.title: The pillow planetarium
missions.description: Create a tiny pretend planetarium on the floor.
steps: Draw paper stars and invent three constellations.
Arrange them around a comfortable seated spot.
Give each other a guided tour of your invented sky.
missions.finish: Your indoor sky has three named constellations.

missions.title: The free-gallery detail duel
missions.supplies: A free gallery or museum collection
missions.description: Find tiny details that could star in a new artwork.
steps: Choose a freely accessible collection and follow its viewing rules.
Each select three details from one or more artworks.
Sketch a new imaginary work combining your selections.
missions.finish: Your detail discoveries have inspired an original concept sketch.
missions.apart: Use the same freely viewable online collection.

missions.title: The two-note theme factory
missions.supplies: Your voice or an instrument you own
missions.description: Make recognizable character themes using only two notes.
steps: Invent a hero, a sneaky neighbor, and a sleepy dragon.
Create a short two-note rhythm for each.
Ask your partner to match themes to characters.
missions.finish: Your three two-note themes can be matched to their characters.
missions.apart: Exchange recordings and character lists.

missions.title: The sock-ball vending machine
missions.supplies: A small box and clean rolled socks
missions.description: Make a pretend vending machine that dispenses one soft parcel.
steps: Create a simple opening in scrap cardboard.
Build a hand-operated chute or sliding door.
Test three gentle deliveries and improve jams.
missions.finish: Your machine dispenses three parcels without getting stuck.

missions.title: The pixel portrait exchange
missions.supplies: A free drawing tool or squared paper
missions.description: Make each other portraits on a sixteen-square pixel grid.
steps: Draw a four-by-four grid with a limited color palette.
Fill its sixteen cells to suggest your partner's expression.
Reveal both portraits and give them art-gallery titles.
missions.finish: Your two sixteen-pixel portraits are complete.
missions.apart: Exchange digital images or photos of your paper grids.

missions.title: Our tiny studio
missions.description: Design an absurdly serious logo for a completely ordinary household object.
steps: Each nominate one object; choose the less glamorous candidate.
One draws its logo while the other invents a slogan; swap halfway.
Present your imaginary brand in a twenty-second pitch.
missions.finish: Your object has a logo, a slogan, and a pitch.
missions.apart: Use the shared hangout canvas or exchange drawings.

missions.title: The map-edge expedition
missions.description: Explore a nearby public place you have noticed on a map but never visited.
missions.supplies: A map and a return route
steps: Each nominate one nearby public place you have never visited; choose one that fits your time.
Follow an agreed route there and each notice one detail you would have missed online.
On the return, name the expedition and draw a tiny route map from memory.
missions.finish: You have visited somewhere new and made a route sketch.

missions.title: The museum of ordinary things
missions.description: Curate five objects as if they belong in a serious museum exhibition.
steps: Each nominate two objects and choose a fifth together.
Write each object a title, an origin story, and one sentence explaining its significance.
Arrange the collection and give each other a guided tour.
missions.finish: Your five-object exhibition has labels and a name.
missions.apart: Each curate a small exhibit and give a live video tour.

missions.title: The game-remix lab
missions.description: Improve a familiar game with one new rule, then see whether it is actually fun.
missions.supplies: A game you already own or a paper game
steps: Pick a short game both of you know and play one normal round.
Each propose one rule change; choose one change to test.
Play a remixed round and agree whether the change stays, changes, or gets retired.
missions.finish: You have tested a rule and written your verdict.
missions.apart: Choose a game you can both play remotely, such as a word or drawing game.

missions.title: The recipe time capsule
missions.description: Turn one improvised dish into a recipe your future selves could really cook.
missions.supplies: Ingredients for a familiar dish and a notes app
steps: Choose a dish you can make from food you already have.
Cook together or in parallel; record the real quantities and timings instead of guessing afterwards.
Give the recipe a title and add one note explaining what you would change next time.
missions.finish: You have a tested recipe with quantities, timings, and a next-time note.
missions.apart: Cook the same dish or a local equivalent and combine your notes.

missions.title: The mini language café
missions.description: Learn enough of a new language to run a tiny pretend café.
missions.supplies: A reliable pronunciation source and paper
steps: Pick a language and learn five useful café phrases from a reliable source.
Make a tiny menu using familiar drinks or snacks and practice the phrases together.
Take turns ordering and serving without reading your notes for one round.
missions.finish: Each of you has completed a short five-phrase café exchange.
missions.apart: Run the café over a call and hold your menu up to the camera.

missions.title: The fifteen-minute better block
missions.description: Leave one familiar public stretch a little nicer than you found it.
missions.supplies: A bag and gloves you already have
steps: Choose a short public route with an ordinary litter bin and a fifteen-minute limit.
Collect only ordinary loose litter you can comfortably pick up; leave sharp or unknown items alone.
Dispose of it appropriately and notice one good detail of the place you helped.
missions.finish: Your chosen stretch is tidier and the collected litter is in a proper bin.

missions.title: The future weekend guide
missions.description: Build a realistic tiny weekend plan around three things you would both enjoy.
steps: Each suggest one place to explore, one thing to make, and one way to rest.
Choose one of each together and check the time, cost, and access details.
Put them into a small weekend plan with one no-spend alternative.
missions.finish: Your three-part weekend plan is practical enough to use.
missions.apart: Make the plan for your next visit or create matching versions in your own areas.

missions.title: The remote director
missions.description: Make a short silent scene in which your partner directs but never touches the props.
missions.supplies: Three everyday objects and a camera or call
steps: Each choose three objects and show them to the other person.
Take turns directing a thirty-second silent story with those objects; give directions before recording.
Watch both scenes and choose one unexpected moment to keep.
missions.finish: Each of you has directed one scene and performed the other.

missions.title: The bench-to-bench relay
missions.description: Carry a story through three nearby public sitting spots.
steps: Choose a comfortable route with places to pause.
Invent a beginning, middle, and ending at successive stops.
Write the final three-part story together.
missions.finish: Your short route has produced a complete story.

missions.title: The tiny food landscape
missions.supplies: Familiar snack pieces and a camera
missions.description: Photograph a snack as though it were a landscape.
steps: Arrange familiar foods into hills, paths, or buildings.
Shoot close to plate level using ordinary light.
Name your edible landscape before sharing the snack.
missions.finish: Your snack landscape has a titled photograph.

missions.title: The two-genre doorway scene
missions.description: Perform the same tiny entrance in two different film genres.
steps: Write one simple line and entrance action.
Perform it first as comedy and then as mystery.
Compare which tiny changes created the new mood.
missions.finish: Your scene has two clearly different genre versions.
missions.apart: Record separate versions and compare them on a call.

missions.title: The pasta-shape tasting club
missions.supplies: Two pasta shapes and familiar sauce
missions.description: Compare how two pasta shapes carry the same sauce.
steps: Cook small portions according to their package directions.
Serve both with the same familiar sauce.
Compare texture and sauce coverage before choosing a favorite.
missions.finish: Your pasta comparison has a recorded preferred shape.

missions.title: The tree-bark pattern studio
missions.description: Draw bark patterns as inspiration for an original design.
steps: Observe three trees from a public accessible path.
Sketch their patterns without rubbing or damaging the bark.
Use one pattern to decorate an imaginary book cover.
missions.finish: Your tree-inspired book cover has an original pattern.
missions.apart: Exchange sketches and compare your chosen patterns.

missions.title: The café board-game corner
missions.supplies: A game you own and your usual drinks
missions.description: Turn one ordinary game into a tiny café session.
steps: Set a small table with your preferred drinks.
Choose a familiar short game and an original café name.
Play one complete round with a café-style welcome.
missions.finish: Your tabletop café has hosted a complete game.

missions.title: The market season detective
missions.supplies: A public market with posted information
missions.description: Find out which seasonal-food claims you can actually verify while browsing.
steps: Agree three foods to look for without planning purchases.
Compare posted origin or harvest information where it is provided.
Write a three-item note separating visible evidence from assumptions about seasonality.
missions.finish: Your market visit produces three honestly verified or unresolved food observations.

missions.title: The weather percussion band
missions.supplies: Paper, hands, and a soft surface
missions.description: Perform an imaginary weather forecast entirely as rhythms.
steps: Choose gentle sounds for sunshine, drizzle, and wind.
Arrange them into a beginning, change, and ending.
Perform your thirty-second forecast without spoken explanation.
missions.finish: Your sound forecast has three distinct weather sections.

missions.title: The paper cup telephone lab
missions.description: Test a simple string telephone in one quiet room.
steps: Make small string holes using suitable normal craft tools.
Connect the cups and hold the string gently taut.
Compare a short phrase with taut and loose string.
missions.finish: Your two conditions have been tested and compared.

missions.title: The public-domain poster remix
missions.supplies: A public-domain image collection and paper
missions.description: Design an original poster inspired by freely usable historic art.
steps: Choose an image clearly marked public domain.
Identify three general colors or shapes you like.
Draw an original event poster using those ideas.
missions.finish: Your fictional event has an original public-domain-inspired poster.
missions.apart: Trade source links and finished poster images.

missions.title: Snack shelf roulette
missions.description: Let a harmless random choice pick your next shared snack.
steps: Choose three suitable options after checking their ingredients.
Assign numbers and draw one without exceeding your budget.
Share the selected snack and invent its tasting award.
missions.finish: Your random snack pick has a joint tasting review.

missions.title: The caption battle
missions.description: Give three photos new lives as movie posters, news stories, and museum exhibits.
steps: Choose three object, pet, or scenery photos from your own camera rolls.
For each photo, write one movie title, one headline, and one museum label together.
Read the captions aloud and crown your favorite.
missions.finish: All three photos have three new captions.
missions.apart: Share the same three photos before starting.

missions.title: The local art critics
missions.description: Curate a tiny art show from three public artworks, murals, or interesting designs.
steps: Choose a public route or free online collection with three artworks or designs.
Each pick a favorite and give a sixty-second explanation of what you notice.
Create a three-piece exhibition title and a one-sentence description of each piece.
missions.finish: Your mini exhibition contains three pieces and a title.
missions.apart: Tour public art in your own areas, then combine the pieces on a call.

missions.title: The six-rule board game
missions.description: Invent a tiny board game you can finish in ten minutes and play it twice.
missions.supplies: Paper, two tokens, and a coin
steps: Sketch a short board and write exactly six rules, including how to win.
Play a test round and note one moment that felt confusing or unfair.
Improve one rule, name the game, and play again.
missions.finish: Your game has six clear rules and a tested second edition.
missions.apart: Draw matching boards and announce coin flips or moves over a call.

missions.title: The silent architect
missions.description: Rebuild your partner's sketch from spoken instructions without seeing the original.
steps: Each draw a little building from ten simple shapes.
Take turns describing your building for two minutes while the other draws; no peeking.
Reveal both pairs and make a third drawing using the funniest accidental features.
missions.finish: You have two comparisons and one jointly designed building.
missions.apart: Exchange only instructions until the reveal over a call.

missions.title: The market curators
missions.description: Design a tiny picnic around one ingredient you would usually walk past.
missions.supplies: A small budget you agree on or food from home
steps: Set a spending cap before you leave and choose one ingredient neither of you usually picks.
Find two simple things that go with it, or use food already at home.
Assemble a small tasting and rate how well the three things work together.
missions.finish: Your three-part tasting has a star ingredient and a verdict.

missions.title: The curiosity rabbit hole
missions.description: Follow one strange everyday question until you can explain it to each other simply.
steps: Pick one question about an ordinary thing, such as why soap bubbles have colors.
Research separately for ten minutes and each bring one reliable source.
Build a sixty-second explanation together, including one thing you still do not know.
missions.finish: You can give a shared explanation and name the sources behind it.
missions.apart: Compare findings on a call or exchange short voice explanations.

missions.title: The helpful how-to
missions.description: Turn something you know into a small guide for someone who actually wants it.
steps: Ask someone you know whether they would like help with one simple task you can explain.
Make a one-page guide using three clear steps and one example; do not include their private information.
Test the guide on each other and offer the improved version to that person.
missions.finish: Your three-step guide has been tested and offered to its intended reader.
missions.apart: Co-write the guide remotely and take turns testing its clarity.

missions.title: The season snapshot
missions.description: Make a six-detail field note of what this particular season feels like.
steps: Each choose two seasonal details from your surroundings and one from your everyday routine.
Combine all six into a page with sketches, photos, or short descriptions.
Date it and choose one detail you would like to check again next month.
missions.finish: You have a dated six-detail season page and a follow-up detail.
missions.apart: Include details from both places, especially if your seasons differ.

missions.title: The window correspondence
missions.description: Turn two different views into a shared illustrated letter.
missions.supplies: Paper or a drawing app and a view
steps: Each sketch a comfortable view from where you are, adding five details rather than aiming for accuracy.
Exchange the sketches and ask about one detail you would never have guessed.
Add a short written reply to the other person's view and date both pages.
missions.finish: Two dated views each have a personal reply.

missions.title: The price-tag-free window draft
missions.supplies: A notebook and a public shopping street
missions.description: Choose objects by usefulness before discovering how their prices influence you.
steps: From public displays each choose three visible objects for specific everyday uses.
Write your preferred pick and reason before reading any visible price tags.
Compare available public prices and discuss whether your ranking changed.
missions.finish: Your pre-price and post-price rankings are both recorded.

missions.title: The six-frame ordinary epic
missions.description: Tell a tiny heroic story in six still photographs.
steps: Choose an object as the hero.
Stage a beginning, challenge, helper, setback, comeback, and finale.
Show the six images without explaining first.
missions.finish: Your partner can follow the six-frame story.
missions.apart: Send separate stories as ordered photo messages.

missions.title: The honest fifteen-second review
missions.supplies: A camera or recorder and an everyday object
missions.description: Make a useful product review with a strict time limit and one actual test.
steps: Choose something you own and agree a harmless practical test.
Record fifteen seconds stating who it helps, its best feature, and one limitation.
Have your partner decide whether the review answers a real purchase question.
missions.finish: Your short review includes a tested use and an honest drawback.
missions.apart: Exchange private review recordings and ask one follow-up question.

missions.title: The rice-ball character kitchen
missions.supplies: Normally prepared rice and familiar toppings
missions.description: Shape small rice snacks into two original characters.
steps: Prepare rice using your usual safe cooking method.
Shape manageable portions with clean hands or utensils.
Add familiar toppings as faces and present the characters.
missions.finish: Your two edible characters are named and ready to eat.

missions.title: The three-minute visitor watch
missions.supplies: Paper and two nearby visible plant patches
missions.description: Compare actual wildlife visits to two plant patches without disturbing either.
steps: Choose two patches visible from a comfortable public or private spot.
Watch each for an equal three minutes and record visits or a genuine zero.
Compare shelter, plant type, and your observation limits without claiming causation.
missions.finish: Your two equal observation windows have honestly recorded results.
missions.apart: Compare your separate field notes rather than pretending the sites are identical.

missions.title: The slow paper puzzle swap
missions.description: Make each other a relaxed three-puzzle page.
steps: Each draw a maze, spot-the-difference, and tiny word puzzle.
Swap the finished pages without giving hints first.
Solve them and discuss the favorite puzzle.
missions.finish: Both homemade puzzle pages have been completed.
missions.apart: Exchange photos and solve on paper or digitally.

missions.title: The public-garden postcard
missions.supplies: A freely accessible garden or park
missions.description: Make an illustrated visitor postcard for a local green space.
steps: Check that entry is free and open.
Each find one detail worth including in a postcard.
Draw a combined design with the place's correct name.
missions.finish: Your outing ends with an original local postcard.

missions.title: The soundtrack scene swap
missions.description: See how different music changes an imaginary scene.
steps: Describe a simple fictional scene together.
Each choose a contrasting accessible piece of music.
Imagine the scene with each and compare its new mood.
missions.finish: Your one scene has two clearly described soundtrack versions.
missions.apart: Play your own accessible copies and compare on a call.

missions.title: The cardboard pinball doodle
missions.supplies: A shallow box, paper ramps, and a paper ball
missions.description: Build a gentle tabletop pinball-style route.
steps: Draw three target zones inside a shallow box.
Add paper ramps and guide a light ball by tilting.
Play five runs and improve one difficult turn.
missions.finish: Your homemade game has five scored test runs.

missions.title: The free short-film scout
missions.description: Curate a tiny two-film festival from accessible short films.
steps: Each choose one legally free film under ten minutes.
Check both can access your choices.
Watch them and award original imaginary prizes.
missions.finish: Your two-film festival has completed both screenings.
missions.apart: Watch on a shared schedule and compare afterward.

missions.title: The picnic coin toss
missions.supplies: Food already at home and a coin
missions.description: Let coin flips choose the details of a tiny nearby picnic.
steps: Choose two suitable public spots and two familiar snack options.
Flip once for the spot and once for the snack.
Enjoy the chosen combination and name your micro picnic.
missions.finish: Your randomly selected picnic has actually happened.

missions.title: Kitchen percussion club
missions.description: Build a tiny rhythm that only needs your hands and two household objects.
steps: One person taps a four-beat pattern with their hands.
The other answers using a different sound; choose comfortable volume.
Alternate for four rounds, then perform a twenty-second finale.
missions.finish: You have one repeatable beat and a finale.
missions.apart: Take turns rather than playing simultaneously, so call delay becomes part of the game.

missions.title: The sound-map expedition
missions.description: Make an audio portrait of a place using five sounds you usually ignore.
steps: Choose a familiar spot and listen quietly for two minutes.
Each identify five different sounds; record objects or ambient sounds only, or write descriptions.
Arrange the sounds into a short journey and guess where each fits.
missions.finish: You have a five-sound portrait of the place.
missions.apart: Record or describe your different surroundings and exchange the sound maps.

missions.title: The comic relay
missions.description: Trade a comic mid-story and see where your partner takes your cliffhanger.
steps: Each draw the first three panels of a six-panel story and end on a cliffhanger.
Swap stories without explaining the intended ending.
Complete the other person's final three panels and reveal both endings.
missions.finish: You have two complete six-panel comics.
missions.apart: Exchange photos of your first three panels before finishing.

missions.title: The memory market
missions.description: Turn twelve household objects into a memory game with one sneaky change.
missions.supplies: Twelve small objects and a cloth
steps: Arrange twelve objects and give your partner thirty seconds to study them.
Cover them, then secretly remove or swap one object before revealing the display.
Trade roles for four rounds and invent a story linking all twelve objects.
missions.finish: You have played four rounds and made one object story.

missions.title: Noodle architecture
missions.description: Turn a bowl of noodles into a playful building challenge, then eat the result.
missions.supplies: Noodles or another familiar base and existing toppings
steps: Agree on a scene to build, such as a garden, a skyline, or an imaginary island.
Prepare your usual food and arrange the toppings to make the scene.
Give each other a tour before eating and choose your favorite tiny detail.
missions.finish: You have made, presented, and eaten your edible scene.
missions.apart: Build the same theme in your own bowls and compare the designs.

missions.title: The first-try workshop
missions.description: Try one small creative skill neither of you already knows.
missions.supplies: Materials you already have and a short tutorial
steps: Choose a skill with a beginner task you can finish today, such as a paper fold or a three-step sketch.
Watch or read one short tutorial, then each make a first attempt without judging it.
Swap one helpful observation and make a second attempt.
missions.finish: You have two attempts each and can describe what improved.
missions.apart: Use the same tutorial and compare first and second attempts over a call.

missions.title: The community discovery desk
missions.description: Find one local free activity you would be glad more people knew about.
missions.supplies: A public noticeboard, library listing, or community website
steps: Each find a free public activity or resource through an official listing.
Check the date, access details, and who might enjoy it.
Make a tiny recommendation with the source link and send it to each other or an interested friend.
missions.finish: You have two checked recommendations someone could actually use.
missions.apart: Find one option near each of you and compare what your areas offer.

missions.title: The micro documentary
missions.description: Make a ninety-second account of a real story only the two of you can tell this way.
steps: Choose one small real event you both remember and each list three details.
Build a beginning, middle, and ending from both lists without pretending your memories are identical.
Record or read a ninety-second version with a title and a closing line.
missions.finish: Your ninety-second story includes details from both of you.
missions.apart: Record alternating parts over a call or exchange clips to play in order.

missions.title: The soundtrack relay
missions.description: Send a musical scene to each other and build a tiny shared soundtrack from the replies.
missions.supplies: Music you already have access to
steps: One person names a scene, such as a sleepy train ride or the final level of a cozy game.
The other chooses a song for it, then sends back a new scene; alternate for six songs.
Put the six choices in order and give your imagined film a title.
missions.finish: Your six-song film soundtrack has a title and scene notes.

missions.title: The impossible-directions walk
missions.supplies: Paper and a familiar public route
missions.description: Guide a familiar route using landmarks while banning its obvious descriptions.
steps: Agree a short accessible route and three forbidden landmark words.
One person gives precise directions without those words.
Swap roles on the return route and score successful arrivals.
missions.finish: Both directions-only routes reach their intended public destination.

missions.title: The reflection self-portrait
missions.supplies: A camera and safe reflective surface
missions.description: Take a creative portrait using an unusual safe reflection.
steps: Choose a spoon, window, or other unbroken reflective surface.
Try three angles without climbing or stretching.
Pick one and give the portrait an art-gallery title.
missions.finish: Your reflection portrait has a chosen final version.
missions.apart: Exchange portraits and guess the reflective surface.

missions.title: The one-take reverse reveal
missions.supplies: A camera and three harmless props
missions.description: Film a scene that appears impossible when played in reverse.
steps: Choose a simple low-motion action such as arranging scattered paper pieces.
Plan a clear final composition and record a controlled take.
Reverse it using a free local editing tool and compare illusion with the original.
missions.finish: Your reverse-played clip creates the intended harmless visual trick.

missions.title: The seasoning correction lab
missions.supplies: A familiar recipe and suitable seasonings
missions.description: Learn which small adjustment improves a familiar dish rather than adding everything at once.
steps: Make a small batch of a normal familiar dish.
Divide a sample and change one suitable seasoning variable in each half.
Taste, compare, and record the smallest change you would repeat.
missions.finish: Your familiar dish has a measured, tested seasoning correction.

missions.title: The shadow clock picnic
missions.supplies: Paper and a stationary safe spot
missions.description: Watch how one shadow changes during a quiet pause.
steps: Choose a comfortable accessible public place.
Sketch the same fixed object's shadow twice twenty minutes apart.
Compare direction and length while enjoying your pause.
missions.finish: Your two dated sketches show a shadow comparison.

missions.title: The illustrated bedtime serial
missions.description: Start a cozy fictional serial with one complete mini episode.
steps: Invent a gentle setting and two recurring characters.
Alternate six illustrated story moments.
End with a satisfying resolution and one future teaser.
missions.finish: Your fictional series has its first complete episode.
missions.apart: Draw alternating panels in shared notes or photo messages.

missions.title: The bookshop title trail
missions.description: Find three book titles that form an accidental story.
steps: Browse respectfully where casual browsing is welcome.
Each nominate titles for a beginning, problem, and ending.
Write your resulting three-title story in your own notes.
missions.finish: Your browsing trip has produced an accidental short story.

missions.title: The humming movie pitch
missions.description: Pitch an original imaginary film through its hummed theme.
steps: Invent a film title without revealing its genre.
Hum an original twenty-second theme for it.
Your partner guesses the genre before your plot reveal.
missions.finish: Both imaginary films have a performed original theme.
missions.apart: Exchange short hummed voice notes.

missions.title: The origami cargo boat test
missions.supplies: Paper, a tray of water, and small coins
missions.description: Compare two small paper boats on a contained water tray.
steps: Fold two different paper-boat designs.
Float them in a shallow tray kept away from electronics.
Add tiny equal loads and record which design holds more.
missions.finish: Your two boat designs have a compared cargo result.

missions.title: The shared cursor-free drawing
missions.supplies: A free drawing tool or paper photos
missions.description: Build a picture by describing changes without pointing.
steps: One draws a simple scene and sends the image.
The other describes three additions entirely in words.
Apply the changes and swap drawing roles.
missions.finish: Your scene has survived two rounds of remote art direction.

missions.title: A constellation for two
missions.description: Turn six dots into a small imaginary constellation with its own story.
steps: One person places six dots without planning a shape.
The other joins them into a constellation; swap for a second drawing.
Name both constellations and invent how people would use them to navigate.
missions.finish: You have two named constellations and their stories.
missions.apart: Exchange photos of the dots or use the shared canvas.

missions.title: Library luck
missions.description: Let a simple clue lead you to a book neither of you would normally choose.
missions.supplies: A public library or your own shelves
steps: Each choose a clue: a color, a number, or an unusual word.
Find one book matching the other person's clue and read a short section to yourself.
Pitch your discoveries in sixty seconds and choose one thing to investigate later.
missions.finish: You have two unexpected books and one shared curiosity.

missions.title: The folded little zine
missions.description: Make a tiny magazine about something you both find unusually interesting.
missions.supplies: One sheet of paper or a notes app
steps: Pick a narrow topic such as good toast, neighborhood cats, or imaginary holidays.
Make six small pages: cover, introduction, two features, an illustration, and a back-cover joke.
Fold or assemble your pages and read the first edition together.
missions.finish: Your six-page zine has a cover and a complete first issue.
missions.apart: Divide the pages between you, then combine photos or a shared document.

missions.title: Mission control
missions.description: Guide a token through a paper maze while your partner is the only one who can see the map.
missions.supplies: Paper, a pen, and a small token
steps: One person draws a simple grid maze with a start, finish, and three named checkpoints.
The other draws a blank grid and moves their token using only the navigator's spoken directions.
Reach the finish, compare routes, and swap roles with a new maze.
missions.finish: Both of you have navigated a complete maze.
missions.apart: Keep the map off-camera and call out directions one at a time.

missions.title: The flavor passport
missions.description: Learn the story of one dish and make a small version with ingredients you can access.
missions.supplies: A recipe and an agreed budget or pantry ingredients
steps: Choose a dish neither of you has made and find a recipe explaining its origin.
Read the recipe together and agree on ingredients or honest substitutions before cooking.
Make it, taste it, and write one thing you learned alongside your recipe source.
missions.finish: You have tried a new dish and kept its recipe source and one discovery.
missions.apart: Cook in parallel or split researching and cooking roles over a call.

missions.title: The tiny invention bureau
missions.description: Prototype a fix for one harmless everyday annoyance using things you already own.
missions.supplies: Scrap materials or a drawing tool
steps: Each name one small annoyance, such as losing bookmarks or tangled charging cables.
Choose one problem and sketch three possible fixes before building anything.
Make the simplest prototype and test whether it helps for two minutes.
missions.finish: You have one tested prototype and a note about what to improve.
missions.apart: Each build a version or split designing and testing roles.

missions.title: The second-life kit
missions.description: Give two useful objects a new home with a clear, respectful handoff.
missions.supplies: Two clean, useful items you own and no longer need
steps: Each choose one item you can genuinely part with; check that it is usable.
Find a willing recipient or an organization that currently accepts those items.
Clean or organize them and arrange the handoff according to the recipient's instructions.
missions.finish: Both items have a confirmed destination and a handoff plan.

missions.title: A postcard from someday
missions.description: Draw a hopeful future day and turn one detail into a real next step.
steps: Each sketch a scene from an ordinary future day you would enjoy, using five small details.
Show your scenes and choose one detail you would both like to make real.
Write a doable first step and keep it with your drawings or in your dream jar.
missions.finish: Your two future-day postcards have one shared next step.
missions.apart: Share the drawings on a call and choose the step together.

missions.title: The next-visit mini map
missions.description: Plan a small part of your next visit so there is something concrete to look forward to.
missions.supplies: A map, notes, or your date planner
steps: Each propose two local stops: one favorite and one new place, including a no-spend option.
Choose a three-stop route and check opening hours, travel time, and any agreed budget.
Name your route and save it with one flexible time window rather than a rigid itinerary.
missions.finish: Your next-visit route has three checked stops and a flexible time window.

missions.title: The public-object redesign brief
missions.description: Find a small usability problem in a public object and propose one improvement.
steps: Observe a bench, sign, or bin from a public path without altering it.
Name one user need and one real constraint such as space or visibility.
Sketch a minimal change and let your partner challenge its tradeoff.
missions.finish: Your proposed redesign states a specific need, constraint, and drawback.
missions.apart: Trade observations from your separate areas and critique the sketches.

missions.title: The one-chair fashion shoot
missions.description: Create three different photo moods using one ordinary chair.
steps: Place the chair securely on a level floor.
Try three comfortable seated poses with different expressions.
Select one image for each mood together.
missions.finish: Your chair shoot has three distinct selected portraits.

missions.title: The object romance short
missions.supplies: Two household objects and a camera
missions.description: Tell a sweet fictional story using two inanimate objects.
steps: Choose two props and give them personalities.
Film a meeting, misunderstanding, and reunion.
Add spoken narration and an original title.
missions.finish: Your two-object story has three complete scenes.

missions.title: The dumpling-fold practice
missions.supplies: Suitable wrappers, a familiar filling, and a reliable recipe
missions.description: Learn two dumpling folds and find which one you can repeat reliably.
steps: Choose a reliable cooking method and ingredients that suit both people.
Practice two beginner folds with equal filling portions.
Cook as directed and compare which folds held their shape.
missions.finish: Both folds have been cooked and tested with a repeatable preferred method.

missions.title: The insect observer sketch
missions.description: Document one tiny creature from a respectful distance.
steps: Observe an insect or spider without handling or baiting it.
Sketch its shape and describe one behavior.
Check a reliable guide if you want an identification.
missions.finish: Your creature record contains a sketch and observed behavior.
missions.apart: Compare observation cards from your separate places.

missions.title: The comfort-show bingo
missions.supplies: A familiar show you can both access
missions.description: Make a friendly bingo card for a familiar episode.
steps: Choose a short episode available to both of you.
Predict nine harmless recurring moments without spoilers.
Watch and compare your marked cards afterward.
missions.finish: Your episode bingo has a completed scorecard.
missions.apart: Start the episode together or compare afterward.

missions.title: The local map swap
missions.description: Guide each other through a familiar public place using drawings.
steps: Choose a small safe area you both know.
Draw a route with three visual landmarks.
Swap maps and walk the routes together.
missions.finish: Both three-landmark hand-drawn maps have been tested.

missions.title: The tiny beatbox lesson
missions.description: Teach each other one simple original vocal rhythm.
steps: Each experiment with three comfortable vocal sounds.
Combine your sounds into a repeating pattern.
Teach your partner and perform one joined rhythm.
missions.finish: Both people can perform the combined pattern.
missions.apart: Teach close-up over a voice or video call.

missions.title: The mechanism you can mime
missions.description: Design a simple mechanism your partner can explain by miming its movement.
steps: Choose a motion such as lifting a lid or turning a pointer.
Draw the input, moving parts, and output with clear arrows.
Have your partner mime the mechanism and fix any unclear connection.
missions.finish: Your mechanism drawing communicates a complete movement chain.
missions.apart: Show diagrams and test the explanation through video.

missions.title: The public-space satellite puzzle
missions.description: Guess public places from broad aerial shapes.
steps: Each select three well-known public parks or landmarks.
Show cropped map views without private addresses.
Guess the places and reveal the wider map afterward.
missions.finish: All six public-place aerial puzzles have been revealed.
missions.apart: Send map crops and reveal links by message.

missions.title: The ten-minute lesson lottery
missions.description: Randomly choose a tiny new skill and actually try it.
steps: Each nominate an accessible ten-minute tutorial using available materials.
Draw one option and follow it together.
Make or demonstrate your first beginner attempt.
missions.finish: Your random lesson has produced a real first attempt.
missions.apart: Use the same tutorial and compare attempts over video.

missions.title: The backwards portrait
missions.description: Draw each other while looking only at the person.
steps: Keep your eyes off your paper.
Draw for sixty seconds without lifting your pen.
Reveal both portraits and sign them like masterpieces.
missions.finish: Two magnificently inaccurate portraits are finished.
missions.apart: Draw from your partner's video feed.

missions.title: The alphabet block hunt
missions.description: Find the alphabet hiding in your neighborhood.
steps: Choose a short familiar public route.
Collect letters from signs without using the same sign twice.
Compare your collection and creatively solve missing letters.
missions.finish: You have collected at least fifteen different letters.
missions.apart: Hunt on separate routes and combine your letters.

missions.title: The fold-flat reading lamp
missions.supplies: Scrap cardboard, paper, and a cool LED light
missions.description: Build a removable paper shade that casts a deliberate pattern.
steps: Sketch a simple pattern and cut it into a freestanding paper panel.
Stand it near a cool LED light without attaching or covering the light.
Adjust distance until the shadow matches your intended design.
missions.finish: Your panel projects a recognizable pattern and packs flat.
missions.apart: Show the projected patterns on video and trade one improvement.

missions.title: The paper island landing
missions.description: Land a sliding coin on increasingly tiny paper islands.
steps: Place three paper islands across a clear table.
Take turns sliding a coin toward each island.
Shrink the islands after both players land successfully.
missions.finish: You have completed three rounds of island landings.

missions.title: The three-dip flight
missions.description: Curate a tasting flight from three dips you already have.
steps: Choose familiar foods that suit both of you.
Serve tiny portions and name each pairing.
Score texture and favorite combination before comparing notes.
missions.finish: Your tasting flight has one jointly chosen winner.

missions.title: The knot school
missions.description: Teach each other one useful knot and test it.
steps: Find clear instructions for two simple everyday knots.
