Each learn one and demonstrate it slowly.
Swap knots and check whether both hold as intended.
missions.finish: Both people can tie both chosen knots.
missions.apart: Teach close-up over video with separate cords.

missions.title: The tiny kindness arcade
missions.description: Build a paper arcade that dispenses small thoughtful favors.
steps: Draw three buttons for easy favors you can offer.
Make a paper ticket for each button.
Take turns choosing a ticket and delivering the favor.
missions.finish: Your arcade has fulfilled one ticket for each person.

missions.title: The version-one memory replay
missions.description: Record two independent accounts of the same ordinary shared moment.
steps: Choose a specific moment without discussing its details first.
Each record what happened, what you noticed, and one uncertain detail.
Compare accounts and preserve both versions rather than forcing one official story.
missions.finish: Your shared moment has two independently recorded viewpoints.
missions.apart: Send your accounts simultaneously before reading each other's.

missions.title: The two-room escape chain
missions.description: Build a puzzle where the final answer needs clues from both rooms.
steps: Each create two fair picture or word clues in your own space.
Exchange clue images without explaining their answers.
Combine the four solved clues into one agreed final phrase.
missions.finish: Both people contribute necessary clues to a solved final answer.

missions.title: The left-turn mini tour
missions.description: Make a tiny exploratory route with three planned left turns.
steps: Use a map to choose a short public route.
Check it stays in familiar accessible areas before starting.
Walk it and choose one unexpected detail to record.
missions.finish: Your prechecked route ends with one new discovery.

missions.title: The paper-cutout visitor
missions.supplies: Paper, a pen, and a camera
missions.description: Take an original paper character on a tiny photo trip.
steps: Draw and cut out a simple character.
Photograph it in three safe nearby settings.
Add a one-line travel diary to each image.
missions.finish: Your paper visitor has a three-stop photo diary.
missions.apart: Send your visitors' diaries to each other.

missions.title: The silent subtitle mismatch
missions.supplies: A camera or your own short clip
missions.description: Give one silent performance two believable but different subtitle tracks.
steps: Record a harmless twenty-second interaction or use your own suitable footage.
Write two subtitle versions that fit the same visible expressions.
Watch both and identify which visual moment supports both meanings.
missions.finish: Your one performance supports two complete subtitle interpretations.
missions.apart: Exchange silent clips and write the two subtitle tracks remotely.

missions.title: The no-bake sandwich dessert
missions.description: Invent a tiny no-bake dessert sandwich.
steps: Choose fillings and crackers you normally eat.
Make two small versions with one difference.
Taste both and write down the winning combination.
missions.finish: Your dessert sandwich has a repeatable winning recipe.
missions.apart: Reveal your versions and compare recipe notes.

missions.title: The miniature mountain vista
missions.description: Draw a tiny natural detail as an enormous landscape.
steps: Find a rock or root visible from a public path.
Imagine its ridges as mountains or valleys.
Sketch a fictional explorer traveling through the landscape.
missions.finish: Your overlooked detail has become an illustrated mountain world.

missions.title: The unfinished-project rescue
missions.supplies: A small creative project and its existing materials
missions.description: Make real progress on a neglected creative project without turning the evening into chores.
steps: Each bring one unfinished drawing, craft, puzzle, or personal creative project.
Choose a concrete twenty-minute finish line the other person can help with.
Work together, then photograph the actual before-and-after difference.
missions.finish: Both projects reach one agreed, visible checkpoint.

missions.title: The shopfront design prediction
missions.description: Predict what a shopfront communicates before checking its actual purpose.
steps: Pick a public-facing frontage without reading its name first.
Each infer the likely purpose from lettering, layout, and materials.
Check the public sign and identify which clue helped or misled you.
missions.finish: Your design reading has a checked purpose and two explained clues.
missions.apart: Exchange public frontage photos before revealing the sign.

missions.title: The rhythm-without-the-tune quiz
missions.description: Identify a familiar song from its rhythm without hearing its melody.
steps: Each choose three songs both people know.
Tap or clap a short distinctive rhythmic phrase without singing.
Allow one extra rhythm clue before revealing the song title.
missions.finish: Six rhythm clues have been guessed and revealed.
missions.apart: Exchange gentle tapping audio clips without lyrics or melody.

missions.title: The paper rocket landing pad
missions.description: Build a tiny landing game for gently tossed paper rockets.
steps: Fold a soft paper rocket and draw three target zones.
Use a clear low tabletop or floor target area.
Take five gentle attempts and improve your landing-pad layout.
missions.finish: Your landing game has five scored trials.

missions.title: The free sound-library story
missions.supplies: A sound library with clear listening access
missions.description: Tell a tiny fictional story through three freely listenable sounds.
steps: Choose a library that clearly labels access and licenses.
Select three harmless sounds you can both play.
Describe a story connecting them in sequence.
missions.finish: Your three sound choices form one complete fictional story.
missions.apart: Exchange sound-page links and compare imagined stories.

missions.title: The postcard thrift hunt
missions.supplies: A small agreed budget and a secondhand shop
missions.description: Find one small secondhand treasure with a story you want to keep.
steps: Agree a modest limit and one useful item category.
Browse together and choose one suitable item within the limit.
Make a dated illustrated card about its new chapter.
missions.finish: Your found treasure has a new home and a souvenir card.

missions.title: Sock puppet newsflash
missions.description: Break an absurd news story using sock presenters.
steps: Give each sock a reporter name.
Report a household event as breaking news.
End with an interview between your two reporters.
missions.finish: Your socks have delivered one complete news bulletin.
missions.apart: Put both puppet reporters on a call.

missions.title: The accidental postcard
missions.description: Turn an ordinary local view into a travel postcard.
steps: Find a public spot you usually walk past.
Frame it as though you are visiting on holiday.
Write a dramatic postcard caption for the view.
missions.finish: Your neighborhood has its own holiday postcard.
missions.apart: Exchange postcards from your separate neighborhoods.

missions.title: The cardboard camera
missions.description: Build a pretend camera that frames surprisingly good scenes.
steps: Cut a viewing window in scrap cardboard.
Decorate it with invented camera controls.
Take turns framing three scenes through the window.
missions.finish: Your cardboard camera has produced three chosen compositions.

missions.title: The alphabet duel
missions.description: Survive a conversation where each sentence starts with the next letter.
steps: Choose a scene such as a haunted bakery.
Alternate sentences from A onward without planning.
Restart once and see how far you get.
missions.finish: Your improvised scene reaches at least letter M.
missions.apart: Play by voice call or alternating messages.

missions.title: The texture triangle
missions.description: Design one snack bite balancing crisp, creamy, and fresh textures.
steps: Choose suitable familiar ingredients that cover the three textures.
Make two small versions with a single proportion changed.
Taste both and write a repeatable recipe for the preferred version.
missions.finish: Your final snack balances all three textures in a recorded ratio.
missions.apart: Compare your two versions and trade the winning recipes.

missions.title: The sky you can recognize
missions.supplies: A reliable star chart and paper
missions.description: Learn a sky pattern well enough to recognize it without its label.
steps: Choose a constellation visible on a reliable chart for your region or season.
Study its main points, hide the label, and redraw the pattern.
Compare it with the chart and teach your partner one dependable locating clue.
missions.finish: Both people can match the selected pattern to a labeled chart.
missions.apart: Use the same chart together without needing a clear night.

missions.title: The encouraging fortune bakery
missions.description: Fold a batch of tiny encouraging paper fortunes.
steps: Each write four specific encouraging fortunes.
Fold them into little paper packets.
Take turns opening and reading one at random.
missions.finish: Your fortune batch contains eight original little messages.
missions.apart: Swap fortune photos with the messages initially hidden.

missions.title: The exact-day sound-and-sight pair
missions.supplies: A camera or sketchbook and optional recorder
missions.description: Keep one visual detail and one sound that belong to this exact day.
steps: Choose a safe ordinary viewpoint and notice something date-specific.
Make one image and describe or record one nonprivate ambient sound.
Label both with the date and the detail you expect to forget.
missions.finish: Your dated pair preserves a specific observation and its sound context.
missions.apart: Exchange your two-part records from the same day.

missions.title: The remote prop mystery
missions.description: Solve a fictional mystery using clues from both rooms.
steps: Each choose three objects as evidence.
Invent a case that requires all six objects.
Take turns adding clues until the case is solved.
missions.finish: Your six-prop mystery has a joint explanation.

missions.title: The tiny-vs-tall hunt
missions.description: Find three amusing size contrasts along a public route.
steps: Look for small and large versions of a similar shape.
Frame each pair from a safe stationary spot.
Name your most dramatic size mismatch.
missions.finish: Your collection contains three clear size contrasts.
missions.apart: Exchange contrast pairs from your separate walks.

missions.title: The invisible-person portrait
missions.description: Make a portrait of yourself without showing your face.
steps: Choose five objects that represent your current interests.
Arrange them thoughtfully in one frame.
Let your partner explain the story they see.
missions.finish: Your five-object portrait has been interpreted.
missions.apart: Exchange the images before discussing their objects.

missions.title: The dramatic instruction video
missions.supplies: A camera and an everyday task
missions.description: Make an epic tutorial for a wonderfully ordinary action.
steps: Choose something simple such as folding a napkin.
Record three overdramatic instructional shots.
Add a grand introduction and final reveal.
missions.finish: Your tiny action has an unnecessarily cinematic tutorial.
missions.apart: Exchange finished tutorials privately.

missions.title: The leftovers-to-lunch challenge
missions.supplies: Properly stored food and familiar pantry ingredients
missions.description: Make a real next-day lunch with a flavor different from the original meal.
steps: Choose suitable safely stored ingredients and a normal preparation method.
Agree one clear change in texture or flavor before starting.
Prepare a small lunch portion and write its short repeatable method.
missions.finish: Your original ingredients become a tested, distinctly different lunch.

missions.title: The wind ribbon observation
missions.supplies: A short ribbon held in your hand
missions.description: Observe the wind with a ribbon you keep hold of.
steps: Choose a calm safe outdoor spot.
Hold the ribbon briefly in three nearby positions.
Sketch which direction it points in each position.
missions.finish: Your three-position wind sketch is complete.

missions.title: The six-clue sofa tournament
missions.description: Make six small original puzzles using your partner's interests as the raw material.
steps: Each create a word clue, picture clue, and short logic clue with checked answers.
Exchange the six clues without revealing which you expect to be hardest.
Solve together and improve one clue that needed an unintended hint.
missions.finish: All six puzzles have a checked solution and one improved clue.
missions.apart: Exchange clue photos and solve them on a call.

missions.title: The free-event mini scout
missions.description: Try a small free public event you would usually overlook.
steps: Check the official time, access, and any booking requirement.
Agree one suitable event or free public display.
Visit and each record one genuinely interesting detail.
missions.finish: Your event visit has two kept discoveries.

missions.title: The spoon-and-paper overture
missions.supplies: A wooden spoon and scrap paper
missions.description: Make a tiny musical introduction using two gentle sounds.
steps: Choose a soft tapping surface and crinkling paper.
Write a simple eight-beat pattern as symbols.
Perform it three times with a grand conductor's gesture.
missions.finish: Your eight-beat overture can be repeated accurately.

missions.title: The cardboard puppet elevator
missions.supplies: A box, string, tape, and a paper character
missions.description: Build a tiny manually operated lift for a paper guest.
steps: Draw two floors inside a small scrap box.
Make a paper platform raised by a hand-held string.
Carry the guest between floors three times.
missions.finish: Your tiny elevator completes three controlled journeys.

missions.title: The virtual architecture tour
missions.description: Explore a building you can visit freely online.
steps: Choose an official tour that needs no payment or account.
Each find one interesting structural or decorative detail.
Sketch a tiny room inspired by both discoveries.
missions.finish: Your tour has inspired one original room concept.
missions.apart: Explore the same tour during a call.

missions.title: The zero-budget tour guide
missions.description: Take turns giving a tiny free tour of a familiar place.
steps: Each choose one publicly accessible nearby spot.
Prepare two actual details without making up local history.
Visit both and deliver your two-minute tours.
missions.finish: Both people have led a complete little local tour.

missions.title: The three-line repair shop
missions.supplies: A pen and two scrap sheets
missions.description: Draw a broken machine; your partner must fix it using only three new lines.
steps: Each sketch a machine with one obvious fault.
Swap drawings and add exactly three repair lines.
Explain why the repaired machine now works.
missions.finish: Both machines have a three-line repair and an explanation.
missions.apart: Trade drawing photos and mark repairs digitally.

missions.title: The texture detective walk
missions.description: Find six contrasting textures without collecting anything.
steps: Look for smooth, rough, soft-looking, shiny, cracked, and patterned.
Photograph or sketch each without disturbing the surface.
Arrange your finds into a tiny texture gallery.
missions.finish: Your gallery contains all six textures.
missions.apart: Combine three textures from each person's route.

missions.title: The bottle-cap mosaic
missions.supplies: Clean caps or colored paper scraps
missions.description: Make a temporary mosaic with a hidden symbol.
steps: Choose a simple creature or landscape.
Arrange clean caps or paper pieces without glue.
Hide a small symbol for your partner to find.
missions.finish: Your mosaic is complete and its secret is discovered.

missions.title: The doodle decoding bureau
missions.description: Invent picture codes and solve each other's secret messages.
steps: Create symbols for six everyday words.
Write a short message using only your symbols.
Trade your key and decode your partner's message.
missions.finish: Both secret picture messages have been decoded.
missions.apart: Exchange photos of your code keys and messages.

missions.title: The tea timing experiment
missions.supplies: Your usual tea or other steeped drink
missions.description: Find how one controlled preparation change affects your familiar drink.
steps: Use the same tea, water amount, and comfortable normal method.
Prepare two samples changing only a recommended steeping time.
Compare aroma and taste before recording your preferred method.
missions.finish: You have tested one variable and saved a specific preparation preference.
missions.apart: Compare separate experiments using the tea you each normally drink.

missions.title: The five-word field course
missions.description: Learn five useful words and use them in a mini scene.
steps: Choose a language and check pronunciation from a reliable source.
Each practice five useful everyday words.
Perform a short café or travel scene using them.
missions.finish: Both people have used all five words aloud.
missions.apart: Rehearse and perform the scene on a call.

missions.title: The book recommendation jacket
missions.supplies: Paper and a book you know
missions.description: Make a new dust jacket recommending a beloved book.
steps: Choose a book you can describe honestly.
Draw a fresh cover and write a spoiler-free recommendation.
Present it to your partner as a bookstore display.
missions.finish: Your book has a handmade recommendation jacket.
missions.apart: Reveal your jackets on a call.

missions.title: The object with two histories
missions.supplies: An object connected to a shared experience
missions.description: Discover which part of a shared object's story each person remembers differently.
steps: Choose an ordinary object associated with a real shared moment.
Each privately write when it mattered and one detail only you noticed.
Read both histories and attach the two accounts to a photo of the object.
missions.finish: Your object has two preserved personal histories.
missions.apart: Use a shared object photo and exchange accounts privately.

missions.title: The shared doodle relay
missions.supplies: Paper and a camera or free drawing tool
missions.description: Build one picture through alternating remote additions.
steps: Start a scene with three simple lines.
Exchange images and add one feature per turn.
Finish after eight turns and name the scene.
missions.finish: Your eight-turn drawing has a completed shared scene.

missions.title: The public pattern league
missions.description: Find repeating patterns that could belong in a game.
steps: Look for three public details with repeated shapes.
Sketch each as a possible game board.
Invent one movement rule for the most interesting pattern.
missions.finish: Your chosen street pattern has a playable movement rule.
missions.apart: Trade patterns and invent rules for each other's finds.

missions.title: The crop that changes the story
missions.supplies: A camera and a scene you can freely photograph
missions.description: Take one photograph that tells two different stories depending on its crop.
steps: Stage or choose a harmless scene with a revealing detail at its edge.
Make a tight crop and a wider crop from the same image.
Let your partner interpret the first before seeing the full scene.
missions.finish: Your two crops produce a clear before-and-after interpretation.
missions.apart: Send the tight crop first and reveal the wide view afterward.

missions.title: The radio mystery in a minute
missions.description: Create a one-minute mystery using voices and harmless sounds.
steps: Invent a missing object and two clues.
Record dialogue with three simple sound effects.
Reveal a fair solution before the minute ends.
missions.finish: Your audio mystery has a beginning and solved ending.
missions.apart: Record alternating dialogue segments remotely.

missions.title: The mini soup garnish bar
missions.supplies: A familiar soup and suitable toppings
missions.description: Turn a bowl of soup into a tiny custom tasting bar.
steps: Prepare a soup you already know how to make.
Offer three familiar toppings in small separate portions.
Try two combinations and choose your house special.
missions.finish: Your soup bar has a tested favorite topping combination.

missions.title: The outdoor symmetry hunt
missions.description: Find three different kinds of natural near-symmetry.
steps: Look at leaves, flowers, or tree shapes without touching.
Sketch or photograph three promising examples.
Compare where each symmetry is slightly imperfect.
missions.finish: Your collection contains three observed symmetry examples.
missions.apart: Exchange examples and notice their little differences.

missions.title: The mini jigsaw lounge
missions.supplies: A puzzle you own or a handmade picture puzzle
missions.description: Host a tiny puzzle lounge with an original house rule.
steps: Choose a manageable puzzle or cut a drawn picture into pieces.
Add a playful rule such as alternating pieces.
Finish it together and name your puzzle lounge.
missions.finish: Your lounge has completed one whole puzzle.

missions.title: The thrift-shop imaginary film set
missions.supplies: A shop where browsing is welcome
missions.description: Cast three browsed objects in an imaginary film scene.
steps: Follow the shop's rules and leave items in place.
Choose three visible objects as fictional props.
Sketch the film scene and invent its title.
missions.finish: Your browsing trip has inspired a three-prop fictional scene.

missions.title: The melody postcard
missions.description: Send an original twenty-second melody inspired by a place.
steps: Choose a real or imaginary place you both know.
Hum a gentle original melody suggesting its mood.
Record it and reveal the place after a guess.
missions.finish: Your place-inspired melody has been recorded and interpreted.
missions.apart: Exchange the labeled melody recordings privately.

missions.title: The cardboard balance bird
missions.supplies: Cardboard, paper clips, and suitable craft tools
missions.description: Build a small shape that balances on one marked point.
steps: Cut a simple symmetrical cardboard bird using a reliable craft guide.
Use adjustable paper clips as small counterweights.
Move the weights until the bird balances at the intended low support point.
missions.finish: Your cardboard shape balances and you can explain the weight adjustment.

missions.title: The emoji-only treasure tale
missions.description: Tell a fictional treasure hunt using only twelve emoji.
steps: Choose a simple adventure with a clear ending.
Encode it as twelve emoji without explanatory text.
Trade interpretations and then reveal the intended story.
missions.finish: Both twelve-emoji adventures have been interpreted.
missions.apart: Send the emoji stories as messages.

missions.title: The cereal-box trailer
missions.description: Pitch a dramatic film starring your breakfast.
steps: Choose a package as the lead character.
Invent its enemy and impossible mission.
Perform a thirty-second trailer with sound effects.
missions.finish: Your household blockbuster has its first trailer.
missions.apart: Take turns performing on a call.

missions.title: The shortest route showdown
missions.description: Take two different public routes to the same nearby meeting point.
steps: Choose an accessible meeting spot ten minutes away and keep phones available.
Each predict which route has more interesting details.
Walk separately, meet, and compare three discoveries each.
missions.finish: You have tested two routes and chosen one for the return trip.

missions.title: The pocket puzzle booklet
missions.description: Make a four-page booklet containing three solvable original puzzles.
steps: Fold a small booklet and choose one shared theme.
Add a picture clue, a word clue, and a final answer using both.
Swap booklets and fix any clue that has two unintended answers.
missions.finish: Both three-puzzle booklets have a checked solution.
missions.apart: Exchange page photos in order without including the solutions.

missions.title: The cushion bowling alley
missions.description: Run a tiny bowling tournament with soft equipment.
steps: Stand three cushions or soft toys as pins.
Roll a sock ball from a marked starting line.
Play five frames and invent a trick-shot bonus.
missions.finish: Your five-frame championship has a final score.

missions.title: The breakfast at dusk club
missions.description: Turn ordinary breakfast ingredients into an evening mini café.
steps: Pick two simple breakfast items you both enjoy.
Cook or assemble them together in small portions.
Set a tiny menu and serve each other.
missions.finish: Your evening breakfast café has served two plates.

missions.title: The optical illusion desk
missions.description: Draw two simple optical illusions and compare their effects.
steps: Find instructions for two paper-based visual illusions.
Each draw one carefully and explain the construction.
Swap drawings and discuss which effect is strongest.
missions.finish: Your two handmade illusions have been tested.
missions.apart: Exchange clear photos of the finished illusions.

missions.title: The route comfort field test
missions.supplies: Paper and a familiar public route
missions.description: Test whether a useful local route actually works as described.
steps: Agree what to check: crossings, seating, step-free sections, and return options.
Walk the accessible route and record only what you can verify.
Mark uncertain details clearly and correct your original directions.
missions.finish: Your route note separates checked comfort features from unverified assumptions.

missions.title: The bad-photo hall of fame
missions.description: Celebrate imperfect photos with affectionate gallery titles.
steps: Each choose three photos you are comfortable sharing.
Give them exaggerated art-gallery titles.
Choose a joint favorite for your private hall of fame.
missions.finish: Your gallery has six consented, titled photographs.
missions.apart: Reveal the selected photos in a private call.

missions.title: The same-minute sky club
missions.description: Compare your skies at one agreed minute.
steps: Choose a time you can both pause safely.
Photograph or sketch the sky from a comfortable spot.
Put the views together with location and time labels.
missions.finish: Your paired sky record captures the same minute.

missions.title: The route you can only hear
missions.supplies: Paper and a familiar public place
missions.description: Map one short public route by sound without closing your eyes or recording people.
steps: Walk normally and note three distinctive nonprivate sound locations.
Use the sound notes to describe the route afterward.
Check them against your actual route and correct any misleading cue.
missions.finish: Your short route has three accurately placed sound landmarks.
missions.apart: Describe a familiar public route for your partner to reconstruct on a map.

missions.title: The opposite-angle puzzle
missions.description: Photograph one scene from two contrasting viewpoints.
steps: Choose a location with two easy safe viewpoints.
Each capture a photo without viewing the other's.
Compare what changed and select a shared title.
missions.finish: Your same scene has two contrasting framed interpretations.

missions.title: The paper creature stop-motion
missions.description: Animate a paper creature crossing a tiny drawn world.
steps: Draw a creature and a simple paper backdrop.
Take twelve photos with small movement changes.
View them in order and add a creature voice.
missions.finish: Your creature completes a twelve-frame journey.

missions.title: The pickle-vs-fresh pairing
missions.supplies: A familiar pickled food, its fresh counterpart, and a neutral base
missions.description: Discover how a small acidic addition changes one familiar snack.
steps: Choose suitable foods you already eat and identify the ingredients openly.
Make two tiny versions using the fresh and pickled options.
Compare balance and decide when each pairing works best.
missions.finish: Your two pairings have a clear compared use rather than just a ranking.

missions.title: The tiny habitat postcard
missions.description: Illustrate a habitat you can observe without disturbing it.
steps: Choose a small visible patch of park or garden.
Sketch plants, shelter, and one observed or possible visitor.
Label which details you actually saw.
missions.finish: Your habitat postcard clearly marks its real observations.
missions.apart: Exchange habitat postcards from different places.

missions.title: The book-spine poem café
missions.description: Compose a poem from book titles without moving beyond your shelf.
steps: Choose four to six titles from your own books.
Arrange the titles into a short poem.
Read it aloud with a calm café introduction.
missions.finish: Your book titles form one finished poem.
missions.apart: Exchange title lists or read poems on a call.

missions.title: The useful-stationery field test
missions.supplies: A browsing-friendly shop or your own stationery
missions.description: Choose a practical design by testing how it would handle one real task.
steps: Agree a task such as packing a short trip or planning a recipe.
Compare three visible notebook layouts or items you already own.
Sketch the option you would actually use and explain the tradeoff.
missions.finish: Your chosen design answers a specific task with an acknowledged limitation.

missions.title: The chair choreography studio
missions.supplies: A stable chair and a song you can access
missions.description: Create a tiny seated dance routine.
steps: Choose a comfortable stable chair and a short music section.
Invent four gentle hand or shoulder movements.
Practice the sequence until you can repeat it together.
missions.finish: Your four-move seated routine has a complete performance.
missions.apart: Practice and perform through a video call.

missions.title: The ramp-and-roll comparison
missions.supplies: Books, cardboard, and a soft ball
missions.description: Compare two gentle ramps with different surfaces.
steps: Build low stable ramps on the floor.
Roll the same soft ball down each without pushing.
Record which travels farther and swap surface positions.
missions.finish: Your ramps have completed a fair two-surface comparison.

missions.title: The interface you can guess
missions.supplies: Paper or a free drawing tool
missions.description: Design three control symbols your partner can use without verbal instructions.
steps: Choose a simple imagined tool with three real actions such as start, pause, and reset.
Draw the three symbols without labels and give a concrete use scenario.
Have your partner choose controls, then redesign the least clear symbol.
missions.finish: Your three-symbol interface has been tested and improved once.
missions.apart: Send the symbols and scenario before explaining the intended actions.

missions.title: The floor target pentathlon
missions.supplies: Paper targets and a soft rolled sock
missions.description: Run a five-event target game with your own scoring rules.
steps: Lay five paper targets on a clear floor.
Agree five comfortable throwing positions or styles.
Play one attempt per event and total your scores.
missions.finish: Your homemade five-event target contest has a complete scorecard.

missions.title: Thumbprint creatures
missions.supplies: Paper and washable ink or pencil
missions.description: Turn five tiny marks into a creature collection.
steps: Make five thumbprints or pencil blobs.
Swap papers and add faces, legs, or wings.
Name the oddest creature and its favorite snack.
missions.finish: You have a five-creature field guide.
missions.apart: Send a photo of blobs for digital doodles.

missions.title: The shortest history tour
missions.description: Create a three-minute tour of one local landmark.
steps: Choose a public landmark with an information sign.
Find two verified facts and one visual detail.
Give your partner a three-minute guided tour.
missions.finish: Your tour includes two facts and one discovered detail.
missions.apart: Each guide a landmark through video or photos.

missions.title: The cardboard creature hotel
missions.supplies: A small box and scrap paper
missions.description: Build rooms for three imaginary tiny guests.
steps: Assign each guest a ridiculous special requirement.
Divide a scrap box into three rooms.
Furnish each room with folded-paper features.
missions.finish: Your hotel can accommodate all three fictional guests.

missions.title: The last-word story duel
missions.description: Make a story where each turn begins with the previous word.
steps: Start with one wildly dramatic sentence.
Begin each reply with your partner's final word.
Continue for ten sentences and give it an ending.
missions.finish: Your ten-sentence story has reached its finale.
missions.apart: Alternate voice notes or text messages.

missions.title: The snack texture brackets
missions.description: Run a tasting tournament where each round uses a different criterion.
steps: Choose four suitable familiar foods and announce the round criteria.
Judge the first round on texture and the final on flavor balance.
Explain which contender changed your mind and why.
missions.finish: Your four-entry bracket has a documented final winner.
missions.apart: Run separate brackets and compare the most surprising result.

missions.title: The map legend trap
missions.supplies: A public map legend and paper
missions.description: Design a route whose solution depends on reading five map symbols correctly.
steps: Choose five real symbols from an official map legend.
Draw a small route with two decoy turns that the symbols rule out.
Swap maps and explain the correct route using the legend.
missions.finish: Both symbol-dependent routes have been solved with a stated reason.
missions.apart: Send the maps and use the same official legend remotely.

missions.title: The good-news radio hour
missions.description: Create a short bulletin of verified encouraging discoveries.
steps: Each find one recent constructive story from a reliable source.
Check its date and what actually happened.
Present a two-minute joint radio bulletin with source credits.
missions.finish: Your bulletin contains two checked stories and their sources.
missions.apart: Record separate segments or present together on a call.

missions.title: The three-object day diary
missions.description: Tell the story of your day through three objects.
steps: Choose an object for morning, afternoon, and evening.
Arrange them into a tiny display.
Explain their roles without turning it into a full recap.
missions.finish: Your day has a photographed or sketched three-object diary.
missions.apart: Show your object displays on a call.

missions.title: The long-distance quiz props
missions.description: Guess everyday objects through close-up camera clues.
steps: Each secretly pick five objects from your own room.
Show only a small detail of each through video.
Reveal the whole object after three guesses.
missions.finish: All ten mystery objects have been revealed.

missions.title: The find-your-initials route
missions.description: Collect your initials from shapes that are not printed letters.
steps: Look for railings, branches, and other public-facing forms resembling each initial.
Capture or sketch the best match for both people.
Combine the shapes into one paired image without altering the scene.
missions.finish: Both initials are represented by actual found shapes rather than lettering.
missions.apart: Each find one person's initials and exchange your paired images.

missions.title: The pocket studio product shot
missions.supplies: Paper backdrop, an object, and a camera
missions.description: Make an ordinary object look like a fancy product launch.
steps: Curve a sheet of paper as a backdrop.
Light the object with daylight or a cool lamp.
Take a polished photo and invent its grand product name.
missions.finish: Your object has a finished pretend launch photograph.
missions.apart: Exchange product shots and pitch the imaginary products.

missions.title: The terrible advertisement agency
missions.description: Advertise a product with the most unhelpful feature imaginable.
steps: Choose an object and invent its silly disadvantage.
Plan a catchy slogan and demonstration.
Perform a thirty-second advert with a confident narrator.
missions.finish: Your useless product has a finished original advert.
missions.apart: Pitch your adverts to each other on a call.

missions.title: The breakfast handoff test
missions.description: Make each other's usual breakfast accurately from a short practical briefing.
steps: Each describe your normal breakfast and one detail that matters.
Prepare the other person's version using suitable available ingredients.
Taste together and identify the briefing detail that made the biggest difference.
missions.finish: Both breakfasts have been prepared and one useful preference learned.

missions.title: The moon-window log
missions.supplies: Paper and a safe sky view
missions.description: Make a paired observation card for the moon or night sky.
steps: Look from a comfortable stationary spot without going anywhere remote.
Sketch the moon or record why it is not visible.
Add the date, time, and one visible sky detail.
missions.finish: Your night-sky card contains a dated honest observation.
missions.apart: Compare your sky cards from your separate windows.

missions.title: The one-page reading exchange
missions.supplies: A book or legally free text each can access
missions.description: Find out what the other person notices in a page you would both normally skim.
steps: Each choose one short passage you are comfortable sharing through normal access.
Read separately and privately select one surprising detail and one unanswered question.
Compare your selections before explaining why you chose the passage.
missions.finish: Both passages have two distinct reader observations.
missions.apart: Read your own accessible copies and discuss on a call.

missions.title: The public mural story route
missions.description: Connect two accessible public artworks with an invented story.
steps: Find two nearby works visible from public places.
Walk a checked comfortable route between them.
Write a fictional bridge scene linking their visual details.
missions.finish: Your two-artwork route has an original connecting story.

missions.title: The fade-to-silence beat test
missions.supplies: An accessible track and a timer
missions.description: Test whether you can keep a beat after the music disappears.
steps: Choose a clear steady beat and tap along for ten seconds.
Pause playback while one person keeps tapping for another twenty seconds.
Restart and compare where the tapping lands, then switch roles.
missions.finish: Both people have tested one uninterrupted beat estimate through silence.
missions.apart: Try separately with the same accessible track and compare recordings privately.

missions.title: The two-sheet suspension sketch
missions.description: Design a fantasy bridge under a silly materials constraint.
steps: Agree two imaginary materials such as clouds and noodles.
Each draw a bridge using only those materials.
Explain its clever feature and spectacular weakness.
missions.finish: Both impossible bridges have an explained concept drawing.
missions.apart: Present your designs through video or photo messages.

missions.title: The free-library opening line tour
missions.description: Discover three very different public-domain book openings.
steps: Choose three books clearly available for free public access.
Read a short opening from each privately.
Draw a tiny bookmark for the one you want to continue.
missions.finish: Your reading tour ends with a chosen book and bookmark.
missions.apart: Compare selections and show your bookmarks on a call.

missions.title: The tiny-budget arcade trip
missions.supplies: A fixed small budget and an accessible arcade
missions.description: Try two different arcade games under one agreed spending cap.
steps: Check local opening hours and prices before leaving.
Agree a firm total budget and choose two suitable games.
Play one round each and name your favorite shared moment.
missions.finish: Your arcade visit includes two tried games within the limit.

missions.title: The invisible orchestra
missions.description: Play an entire imaginary orchestra without instruments.
steps: Choose a song you both recognize.
Assign each other three imaginary instruments.
Mime a dramatic performance through the final chorus.
missions.finish: Your imaginary concert reaches its final bow.
missions.apart: Start the song together and perform on video.

missions.title: The view without the view
missions.supplies: Paper and a familiar public route
missions.description: Guide your partner to a public detail using everything except its appearance.
steps: Pick a safe detail along a familiar walking route.
Describe its sound, surroundings, or purpose without naming its color or shape.
Find it together and switch clue-giver roles.
missions.finish: Both deliberately difficult landmark clues have been solved.
missions.apart: Send clues about a shared map view or familiar public place.

missions.title: The paper stained-glass window
missions.description: Design a bright pretend stained-glass panel.
steps: Outline a window divided into bold shapes.
Swap designs and color the other person's sections.
Hold your completed panels beside a light source.
missions.finish: Both original window panels are finished.
missions.apart: Send outlines to color with simple digital tools.

missions.title: The memory swap shop
missions.description: Remember positions and object details in two different challenge rounds.
steps: Arrange nine objects and allow twenty seconds to study them.
First swap two positions; next change one small detail.
Switch roles and compare which kind of change was harder to detect.
missions.finish: Both players have solved a position change and a detail change.

missions.title: The leftover upgrade duel
missions.supplies: Suitable stored leftovers and familiar additions
missions.description: Turn one safely stored leftover into two noticeably different small dishes.
steps: Agree which properly stored food is suitable to reheat or eat.
Each choose a different flavor or texture change using available ingredients.
Prepare, taste, and choose which version deserves repeating.
missions.finish: Two distinct leftover transformations have been prepared and compared.

missions.title: The paper helicopter lab
missions.description: Learn why a paper helicopter spins through testing.
steps: Fold two small paper helicopters using simple instructions.
Drop them from the same low hand height.
Change one blade length and compare the next drop.
missions.finish: Your comparison identifies one change that affects the spin.

missions.title: The skill coupon studio
missions.description: Design a tiny coupon for a skill you can actually share.
steps: Choose something your partner would enjoy learning.
Design a coupon with its lesson and time needed.
Redeem one coupon for a five-minute introduction.
missions.finish: Your skill coupon has delivered its first mini lesson.
missions.apart: Redeem the coupon through a short video lesson.

missions.title: The shared-day newspaper
missions.description: Publish a one-page newspaper about your ordinary day.
steps: Choose a headline and one tiny real story each.
Add a weather box and an entirely silly advertisement.
Read the first edition together.
missions.finish: Your newspaper has a headline, two stories, and an advertisement.
missions.apart: Create separate sections in one shared note.

missions.title: The camera-only repair challenge
missions.supplies: Paper, tape, and one small harmless task
missions.description: Help solve a tiny construction problem without touching your partner's materials.
steps: Each choose a task such as folding a stable phone stand.
The helper can only observe the camera and give precise instructions.
Switch roles and compare which directions prevented the most confusion.
missions.finish: Both partners complete one remotely guided construction task.

missions.title: The no-repeat observation round
missions.supplies: A timer and a safe public viewpoint
missions.description: Keep noticing new details after the obvious ones are used up.
steps: Choose a shared view and alternate naming one directly visible detail.
Ban repeats, interpretations, and details already named.
Continue for twenty observations and compare the first and last discoveries.
missions.finish: Your viewpoint produces twenty distinct, verifiable observations.
missions.apart: Use the same public image or a shared video view.

missions.title: The repeating-shape diptych
missions.description: Connect two unrelated subjects through matching shapes.
steps: Pick a shape such as a circle or zigzag.
Photograph two unrelated things that strongly share it.
Place the photos side by side and title the pair.
missions.finish: Your two-photo artwork reveals one shared shape.
missions.apart: Each contribute one half of the matching pair.

missions.title: The tiny courtroom drama
missions.description: Hold a fictional trial over an extremely small household mystery.
steps: Choose a harmless pretend case involving two props.
Take turns presenting evidence for both sides.
Deliver a fair but ridiculous fictional verdict.
missions.finish: Your imaginary case has evidence and a final verdict.
missions.apart: Present evidence props through your cameras.

missions.title: The three-ingredient cracker lab
missions.supplies: Ingredients for a reliable simple cracker recipe
missions.description: Make a small batch of crackers and test two thicknesses.
steps: Choose a suitable reliable recipe and follow its measurements.
Shape half the batch slightly thinner without changing the ingredients.
Bake as directed and compare crispness after cooling.
missions.finish: Your two thicknesses produce a checked preference and repeatable method.

missions.title: The pebble portrait gallery
missions.description: Draw natural stones as a cast of imaginary characters.
steps: Observe three stones without moving or marking them.
Sketch each with a fictional face on paper.
Write a tiny cast description for your trio.
missions.finish: Your gallery has three stone-inspired original characters.

missions.title: The five-object snug room
missions.description: Design a tiny comfortable corner with only five chosen items.
steps: Agree a safe clear corner at home.
Choose five items for comfort, light, or decoration.
Arrange them and spend ten minutes enjoying the space.
missions.finish: Your five-item corner has hosted its first quiet visit.

missions.title: The new-bench lunch break
missions.description: Give your ordinary packed lunch a tiny new setting.
steps: Choose a suitable nearby public sitting area.
Bring your normal lunch and leave the spot tidy.
Sketch its view and name your imaginary lunch café.
missions.finish: Your ordinary lunch has a new view and café name.

missions.title: The musical mood map
missions.supplies: Paper and music you already access
missions.description: Draw a map while listening to three contrasting short tracks.
steps: Choose three pieces available to both of you.
Draw a different imaginary landscape during each.
Join the landscapes into a three-region musical map.
missions.finish: Your map contains three music-inspired regions.
missions.apart: Compare your separate maps after the same listening sequence.

missions.title: The cardboard goal machine
missions.supplies: A box, tape, and rolled socks
missions.description: Make a tabletop target with three differently sized goals.
steps: Cut or fold three openings in scrap cardboard.
Assign points based on opening size.
Toss soft rolled socks gently for five rounds.
missions.finish: Your homemade goal machine has a completed scorecard.

missions.title: The public transit fantasy route
missions.description: Plan an imaginary route based on interesting station names.
steps: Choose an official map you can view freely.
Pick three stops whose names suggest a fictional story.
Draw the route and tell its tiny imaginary adventure.
missions.finish: Your fictional adventure uses three real mapped stop names.
missions.apart: Compare routes from your separate cities or chosen maps.

missions.title: The ice-cream flavor draft
missions.description: Choose a small treat through a friendly flavor draft.
steps: Check options that suit both people's dietary needs.
Each nominate one flavor within the agreed budget.
Order your chosen portions and compare tasting notes.
missions.finish: Your flavor draft ends with two actual tasting reviews.

missions.title: The secret handshake lab
missions.description: Invent a greeting with five ridiculous movements.
steps: Each contribute two movements.
Add a synchronized finishing pose.
Practice until you complete it twice without stopping.
missions.finish: Your five-part greeting works from memory.
missions.apart: Make a mirrored version across video.

missions.title: The quietest corner contest
missions.description: Compare three public sitting spots by their sounds.
steps: Choose three nearby accessible places to pause.
Listen quietly for one minute at each.
Choose the calmest and give it a secret nickname.
missions.finish: You have a tested favorite pause spot.

missions.title: The travel poster for nowhere
missions.description: Advertise a holiday destination that does not exist.
steps: Invent its landscape and signature local attraction.
Draw a poster using only three colors.
Pitch a weekend there to your partner.
missions.finish: Your imaginary destination has a finished travel poster.
missions.apart: Reveal your posters and take turns pitching.

missions.title: The clue budget auction
missions.description: Guess secret words while bidding for how few clues you will need.
steps: Each prepare five ordinary words with a six-word clue allowance.
The guesser bids one to six clue words before hearing anything.
Score successful guesses by the number of clue words left unused.
missions.finish: Ten word rounds have been played under the agreed clue budget.
missions.apart: Run the clue auction on a voice call or by message.

missions.title: The childhood snack remix
missions.supplies: A familiar snack and pantry extras
missions.description: Give a favorite childhood snack one thoughtful twist.
steps: Choose a snack you can make from available ingredients.
Change just one topping, shape, or presentation.
Taste the original and remix before picking a favorite.
missions.finish: Your childhood snack has a tested new version.
missions.apart: Make separate remixes and trade recipe notes.

missions.title: The coin-history detour
missions.supplies: A coin and a reference source
missions.description: Investigate the tiny artwork on an everyday coin.
steps: Choose a coin and examine its symbols.
Verify one design fact using an official mint or museum source.
Draw an oversized detail and share what you learned.
missions.finish: Your coin has an illustrated fact card.
missions.apart: Compare coins and illustrated details on a call.

missions.title: The free-fun directory
missions.description: Curate three genuinely free local activities for someone new.
steps: Check official venue pages for dates and access details.
Choose three different kinds of free activity.
Make a single illustrated directory page with source links.
missions.finish: Your directory has three checked free suggestions.
missions.apart: Each contribute options from your own area.

missions.title: The ten-second time machine
missions.description: Record a tiny sound souvenir you can revisit later.
steps: Choose a harmless ambient sound from your own space.
Record ten seconds without capturing anyone's private conversation.
Name it with its date and one-line context.
missions.finish: Both sound souvenirs are labeled for future listening.
missions.apart: Exchange the two labeled audio clips privately.

missions.title: The asynchronous mini detective
missions.description: Send a solvable three-clue mystery without needing the same schedule.
steps: Create a fictional culprit and three fair written clues.
Send the clues together with a clear puzzle question.
Exchange solutions and explain how the clues connect.
missions.finish: Both mysteries have a checked solution.

missions.title: The reflected-city gallery
missions.description: Collect three reflections that make your town look different.
steps: Look from public paths at windows or still water.
Capture scenes without including identifiable passersby.
Arrange the three reflections as a tiny gallery.
missions.finish: Your gallery shows three transformed ordinary views.
missions.apart: Combine galleries from both of your locations.

missions.title: The four-seasons tabletop
missions.supplies: Paper props, objects, and a camera
missions.description: Photograph one tabletop scene as four imaginary seasons.
steps: Choose an object to stay fixed in every shot.
Change paper scenery to suggest each season.
Arrange the four finished images in seasonal order.
missions.finish: Your fixed subject has visited all four seasons.

missions.title: The three-sound thriller
missions.description: Tell a suspenseful fictional story using just three gentle sounds.
steps: Choose three safe sounds you can make quietly.
Arrange them to suggest an arrival, problem, and reveal.
Let your partner describe the story they heard.
missions.finish: Your three-sound piece has a shared interpretation.
missions.apart: Exchange sound pieces and trade story interpretations.

missions.title: The flatbread constellation
missions.supplies: A familiar flatbread recipe and toppings
missions.description: Make a tiny edible star map on a flatbread.
steps: Choose a familiar recipe and ingredients you both enjoy.
Arrange toppings as one constellation before normal cooking.
Draw its star lines on paper and compare after cooking.
missions.finish: Your finished flatbread matches its paper constellation.

missions.title: The rain-afterward expedition
missions.description: Notice how a familiar place changes after ordinary rain.
steps: Choose a short accessible route when weather is comfortable.
Look for three changed colors, reflections, or plant details.
Create a three-observation field note.
missions.finish: Your familiar route has an after-rain observation record.

missions.title: The bedtime radio theater
missions.description: Perform a gentle three-scene radio story.
steps: Choose a fictional setting such as a moon bakery.
Make a small problem that resolves kindly.
Perform three scenes with quiet original sound effects.
missions.finish: Your radio story has a complete peaceful ending.
missions.apart: Split the narration and character roles over a call.

missions.title: The library atlas expedition
missions.supplies: A library atlas or free public map collection
missions.description: Plan an entirely imaginary journey from an atlas.
steps: Find a publicly accessible atlas or map collection.
Choose a place neither of you knows well.
Build a three-stop fictional itinerary using checked map labels.
missions.finish: Your atlas expedition has a mapped three-stop itinerary.

missions.title: The body-percussion relay
missions.supplies: Your hands and a soft surface
missions.description: Grow a gentle rhythm one sound at a time.
steps: Start with one comfortable tap or clap.
Alternate adding a sound while repeating the earlier pattern.
Stop at eight sounds and perform the full sequence.
missions.finish: Your shared eight-sound pattern can be repeated.

missions.title: The flat-pack tiny furniture
missions.description: Make two tiny pieces of furniture with slot joints.
steps: Sketch a chair and table as simple separate parts.
Cut suitable slots so pieces slide together.
Test the furniture with a paper character.
missions.finish: Your two-piece miniature room stands without extra supports.

missions.title: The digital evidence trail
missions.supplies: Freely accessible official collection or reference pages
missions.description: Solve one real curiosity question using a short trail of reliable evidence.
steps: Choose a specific question with an answer you can check.
Find three relevant source pages and note what each actually establishes.
Explain your answer with one remaining uncertainty instead of collecting links alone.
missions.finish: Your curiosity question has a three-source answer and a stated limit.
missions.apart: Research different parts and combine the evidence on a call.

missions.title: The public trail sampler
missions.supplies: A checked local public walking route
missions.description: Try one short marked public route you usually overlook.
steps: Choose a comfortable accessible route and check the return path.
Walk a small section at an easy shared pace.
Keep a sketch or photo of one new detail each.
missions.finish: Your route sampler has two recorded discoveries.

missions.title: The one-line monster
missions.description: Create a monster without lifting the pen.
steps: Draw its body in one continuous line.
Your partner adds its habitat in one line.
Give it a warning label and friendly weakness.
missions.finish: Your monster has a home and a warning label.
missions.apart: Trade a photo after the first drawing.

missions.title: The neighborhood time machine
missions.supplies: An old public photograph and a current map
missions.description: Match an archived street photograph to the same present-day view.
steps: Find a dated public archive image of a nearby accessible place.
Locate its viewpoint from a public path or current map imagery.
List three surviving details and three changes you can actually verify.
missions.finish: Your matched views have six checked observations.
missions.apart: Compare archive and current map images together on a call.

missions.title: The fold-and-swap creature
missions.description: Draw one creature without seeing the whole picture.
steps: Fold paper into head, body, and feet sections.
Draw secretly, fold, and exchange at each section.
Unfold and invent the creature's life story.
missions.finish: Your surprise creature has a name and habitat.

missions.title: The tabletop rebound cup
missions.supplies: A coin, paper targets, and a book laid flat
missions.description: Bank a sliding coin off a book edge into a target zone.
steps: Lay a book flat as a low barrier away from the table edge.
Mark three targets that require a single controlled rebound.
Take five turns each and score accuracy rather than force.
missions.finish: Both players complete a scored five-turn rebound round.

missions.title: The two-ingredient canapé
missions.description: Create tiny party bites using only two ingredients each.
steps: Choose ingredients that you already like together.
Each assemble three small bites with different arrangements.
Host a very serious canapé judging ceremony.
missions.finish: Both two-ingredient entries have been sampled.

missions.title: The cloud-type desk
missions.description: Learn to identify one cloud type from a safe viewpoint.
steps: Use a reputable guide to choose one common cloud type.
Observe the sky from a comfortable stationary spot.
Sketch your best match or note why no match appears.
missions.finish: Your sky note includes a sketch and identification attempt.
missions.apart: Compare your different skies and guide matches.

missions.title: The five-minute welcome kit
missions.supplies: Paper and knowledge of a familiar public place
missions.description: Make a first-visit guide that solves three real newcomer questions.
steps: Pick a public place you know and list three things a newcomer might miss.
Verify the entrance, free facilities, and one practical tip from official information.
Have your partner use the guide to answer three test questions.
missions.finish: Your one-page guide answers three tested first-visit questions.
missions.apart: Trade guides for places in your different areas.

missions.title: The chapter opening recording
missions.description: Capture the beginning of a life chapter before you know how it turns out.
steps: Name one real transition currently happening without predicting a perfect outcome.
Each record what is known, what is uncertain, and one ordinary detail of today.
Save both accounts with a date to revisit after the transition.
missions.finish: Your current chapter has two dated, honest opening records.
missions.apart: Send recordings privately and agree a revisit date.

missions.title: The asynchronous sound hunt
missions.supplies: A recorder or written sound descriptions
missions.description: Send three sound clues your partner can answer whenever they are free.
steps: Record or describe three harmless nonprivate sounds without identifying the source.
Send all clues with a promise to reveal only after guesses.
Compare guesses and explain which detail made each source recognizable.
missions.finish: All three sound clues have guesses and a source reveal.

missions.title: The hidden-face neighborhood
missions.description: Find accidental faces in public-facing everyday objects.
steps: Look for face-like shapes in architecture and street details.
Collect three without disturbing anything.
Give each a name and one funny personality trait.
missions.finish: Your neighborhood has three newly discovered imaginary residents.
missions.apart: Trade face finds from separate walks.

missions.title: The dramatic desk detective
missions.supplies: A camera and three harmless props
missions.description: Create a fictional detective scene as one still photograph.
steps: Choose three props as pretend evidence.
Arrange them with one clear visual clue.
Ask your partner to invent the mystery from the photo.
missions.finish: Your staged scene has inspired a solved fictional case.
missions.apart: Send photos and trade detective explanations.

missions.title: The match-cut handoff
missions.supplies: A camera and two differently shaped props
missions.description: Create a clean cut that makes one ordinary object transform into another.
steps: Choose props with one visual feature you can line up.
Keep the camera fixed and film two short matching movements.
Trim at the aligned moment and test whether the transition reads clearly.
missions.finish: Your finished short clip has one intentional match-cut transformation.

missions.title: The smoothie color studio
missions.supplies: Familiar smoothie ingredients and a blender
missions.description: Create a drink inspired by a chosen color palette.
steps: Use ingredients you normally prepare in your blender.
Choose a target color and blend a small portion.
Name the actual result and draw its label.
missions.finish: Your smoothie has an original color-based café identity.
missions.apart: Reveal drinks and compare your target versus final colors.

missions.title: The seed-shape gallery
missions.supplies: Paper and safely visible plants or food seeds
missions.description: Compare seed shapes without collecting unknown plants.
steps: Observe three safe visible examples such as pantry seeds.
Sketch their shape and size relative to each other.
Design an imaginary flying machine inspired by one.
missions.finish: Your seed-inspired machine has a finished concept drawing.
missions.apart: Exchange seed sketches and your machine designs.

missions.title: The tiny indoor camping trip
missions.supplies: Blankets, cushions, and a cool lamp
missions.description: Make an imaginary campsite inside your own home.
steps: Arrange a low safe blanket campsite with clear exits.
Draw a fictional trail map and campsite flag.
Tell a short invented adventure beside a cool lamp.
missions.finish: Your indoor campsite has a flag, map, and story.

missions.title: The one-stop architecture studio
missions.description: Study one public building as inspiration for a tiny fantasy town.
steps: Choose an exterior visible from a public path.
Sketch three distinctive architectural details.
Use them to design an original imaginary town hall.
missions.finish: Your real-world observation has inspired a finished concept drawing.

missions.title: The two-bar rhythm handoff
missions.description: Teach a short rhythm accurately using an agreed written key.
steps: Choose four simple symbols for gentle sounds or rests.
Each write a two-bar pattern and exchange scores.
Perform the other's pattern before hearing the intended version.
missions.finish: Both written rhythm scores have been performed and checked.
missions.apart: Send score photos and short performance recordings.

missions.title: The object rescue bridge
missions.supplies: Paper strips, tape, and two books
missions.description: Build a tabletop walkway for a paper character.
steps: Use two books to define a short gap.
Build a walkway with a small protective railing.
Move your paper character across without the walkway collapsing.
missions.finish: Your paper traveler crosses the completed bridge.

missions.title: The digital postcard chain
missions.supplies: A camera and simple image markup
missions.description: Transform one ordinary photo through three playful remote additions.
steps: Send a photo of an object you are comfortable sharing.
Alternate adding a fictional sign, character, and caption.
Save the final image as your absurd joint postcard.
missions.finish: Your ordinary photo has three coordinated original additions.

missions.title: The homemade photo booth strip
missions.description: Create a four-shot photo strip with a tiny story.
steps: Agree four expressions or simple poses.
Take four timed pictures using a stable camera position.
Arrange them in order and add a dated strip title.
missions.finish: Your four-frame photo strip tells its intended little story.
missions.apart: Each make a strip and combine your best matching frame.

missions.title: The elevator audition
missions.description: Sell an utterly useless invention in thirty seconds.
steps: Choose an ordinary object as your prototype.
Invent a problem that nobody actually has.
Pitch it while your partner acts as a skeptical investor.
missions.finish: Both inventions have received an absurd investment offer.
missions.apart: Take turns pitching on a call.

missions.title: The pocket park expedition
missions.description: Explore the smallest public green space near you.
steps: Choose a nearby park you have never paused in.
Find one impressive tiny detail each.
Draw a simple explorer's map with both discoveries.
missions.finish: You have mapped a pocket park together.

missions.title: The cardboard pinhole viewer
missions.supplies: A box, foil, tape, and tracing paper
missions.description: Build a basic pinhole viewer and find a clear indoor image.
steps: Follow a reputable simple box-viewer guide using available materials.
Test it with a well-lit indoor object; never point it at the sun.
Adjust the screen distance and sketch your sharpest reversed image.
missions.finish: Your viewer produces a visible image you can explain.

missions.title: The hat of impossible jobs
missions.description: Act out occupations that should not exist.
steps: Each write three jobs such as cloud barber.
Draw one and mime a typical working day.
Your partner guesses before you reveal the job.
missions.finish: All six impossible jobs have been demonstrated.
missions.apart: Send job prompts privately and mime over video.

missions.title: The pretend cooking show
missions.supplies: Ingredients for an easy familiar dish
missions.description: Film a short cooking show for a simple snack.
steps: Choose something you already know how to prepare.
Record an introduction, one key step, and the reveal.
Watch the clips while enjoying the finished snack.
missions.finish: Your snack has its own three-part cooking episode.
missions.apart: Each film a segment and exchange finished episodes.

missions.title: The camera-angle lesson
missions.description: Learn how three camera angles change the same subject.
steps: Place an object in good ordinary light.
Take eye-level, low-angle, and overhead photos.
Name the mood each angle creates.
missions.finish: Your three photos demonstrate three different visual moods.
missions.apart: Trade angle sets and guess the intended moods.

missions.title: The game-for-a-younger-self
missions.description: Design a simple game your younger selves would have loved.
steps: Choose an age and a shared imaginative theme.
Write three friendly rules and make a simple board.
Play one short round and improve a confusing rule.
missions.finish: Your child-friendly game has survived a complete playtest.
missions.apart: Play with matching paper boards over a call.

missions.title: The miniature memory map
missions.description: Map a familiar room using moments instead of furniture.
steps: Draw the outline of a room you both know.
Mark three spots with tiny remembered scenes.
Tell each other one detail missing from the map.
missions.finish: Your room map contains three shared scenes.
missions.apart: Draw the same remembered room in separate places.

missions.title: The measured room puzzle
missions.supplies: Paper and three rough room measurements
missions.description: Design a useful small layout change for a space your partner describes.
steps: Share only three measurements and the practical problem to solve.
Sketch a change using existing furniture without buying anything.
Have your partner test the clearances and correct your assumptions.
missions.finish: Your layout proposal has a real fit check and a revised plan.

missions.title: The tiny landmark tournament
missions.description: Choose a champion among three overlooked public details.
steps: Pick categories: charm, weirdness, and story potential.
Nominate three nearby public-facing details.
Score them together and write the winner's citation.
missions.finish: Your overlooked landmark has won a documented title.

missions.title: The five-line photo hunt
missions.description: Collect straight, curved, broken, crossing, and spiral lines.
steps: Choose safe subjects in your own space or public views.
Take one deliberate photograph for each line type.
Arrange them into a five-picture visual alphabet.
missions.finish: Your visual alphabet includes all five line types.
missions.apart: Compare your two line collections remotely.

missions.title: The opening credits studio
missions.supplies: Paper title cards and a camera
missions.description: Make opening credits for an imaginary show about your day.
steps: Invent a show title and three cast roles.
Draw title cards and stage brief prop shots.
Play the sequence with a hummed original theme.
missions.finish: Your day has an original opening-credits sequence.
missions.apart: Each contribute half the credits and watch them together.

missions.title: The mini tasting scorecard
missions.supplies: Three familiar versions of one food
missions.description: Make your own tasting rubric for an everyday favorite.
steps: Choose three suitable samples already available.
Agree three criteria without ranking first.
Taste small portions and compare your scorecards.
missions.finish: Your tasting has a documented winner and explained scores.

missions.title: The shaded-ground comparison
missions.supplies: Paper and an optional suitable thermometer
missions.description: Compare two nearby ground conditions and separate observations from guesses.
steps: Choose accessible shaded and unshaded spots in comfortable weather.
Record visible surface and moisture differences without touching unknown substances.
If using a suitable thermometer, compare readings by the same method.
missions.finish: Your two-site note distinguishes measured results from visual hypotheses.

missions.title: The five-item comfort redesign
missions.supplies: Five existing comfort items and a small space
missions.description: Solve one real comfort problem in a small corner using only five existing items.
steps: Choose a need such as a reading surface or less glare.
Each propose a five-item arrangement without buying anything.
Test the preferred layout for ten minutes and change the least useful item.
missions.finish: Your small space has a tested five-item arrangement with one revision.
missions.apart: Show the space on video and take turns proposing practical layouts.

missions.title: The local postcard challenge
missions.description: Find a postcard-worthy view within an ordinary short outing.
steps: Choose a familiar accessible public destination.
Spend ten minutes finding one distinctive viewpoint.
Sketch a postcard and write a tiny visitor greeting.
missions.finish: Your ordinary destination has an original postcard view.
missions.apart: Trade postcards from your different areas.

missions.title: The kitchen conductor game
missions.description: Perform a piece controlled by invented conductor signals.
steps: Agree gestures for start, stop, soft, and slow.
One conducts while the other makes gentle rhythms.
Swap roles and finish with a synchronized ending.
missions.finish: Both conductors have led one complete tiny performance.

missions.title: The imaginary invention patent
missions.description: Draw an absurd invention as a serious patent application.
steps: Choose a harmless problem that does not really need solving.
Draw labeled components and three operating steps.
Present the patent to your skeptical partner.
missions.finish: Your invention has a complete labeled pretend patent.
missions.apart: Swap patent drawings and review each other's mechanism.

missions.title: The two-time-zone plan test
missions.supplies: A reliable time-zone reference and your actual availability
missions.description: Find a short shared window that works in both people's real local schedules.
steps: Each name two realistic local-time windows for a call or activity.
Convert them using the correct dates and check daylight-saving differences.
Choose one overlap and save its time in both local zones.
missions.finish: Your shared plan has one checked date and matching local times.

missions.title: The beginner footwork session
missions.supplies: A free beginner dance lesson and clear space
missions.description: Learn a short comfortable dance step sequence.
steps: Choose a free beginner tutorial suited to your space.
Practice two basic steps slowly before combining them.
Perform the joined sequence twice at a comfortable pace.
missions.finish: Both people can repeat the two-step sequence.
missions.apart: Follow the same lesson and practice on video.

missions.title: The one-minute forecast
missions.description: Predict each other's next three harmless choices, then test them.
steps: Offer three pairs such as window seat or aisle, crisp or soft.
Write guesses privately before either person answers.
Reveal choices and explain the most surprising mismatch.
missions.finish: All three predictions have been checked without changing the options.
missions.apart: Send your predictions together before revealing answers.

missions.title: The same-view challenge
missions.description: Photograph one public scene in three completely different ways.
steps: Choose a safe place to stand without blocking anyone.
Take a wide shot, close detail, and unusual angle.
Guess which photos belong to the same scene.
missions.finish: Your ordinary scene has three distinct interpretations.
missions.apart: Exchange your three-shot sets before revealing the location.

missions.title: The pattern factory
missions.description: Design a repeat pattern from three simple shapes.
steps: Choose one circle, line, and unusual shape.
Repeat and rotate them across your page.
Trade patterns and invent a product for each.
missions.finish: Both patterns have become imaginary product designs.
missions.apart: Send pattern photos and design each other's product.

missions.title: The twenty-token expedition
missions.supplies: Twenty paper tokens and five household objects
missions.description: Bid on the tools you need to solve a surprise tabletop challenge.
steps: Reveal a goal such as moving a paper ball without touching it.
Auction five possible tools with ten tokens per person.
Try the goal using only the tools you won, then compare designs.
missions.finish: Both players attempt the same goal with their auctioned tools.

missions.title: The left-right topping draft
missions.supplies: Toast or flatbread and familiar toppings
missions.description: Build two snack halves through alternating ingredient picks.
steps: Choose four toppings that suit both of you.
Alternate drafting a topping for each half.
Assemble, share, and compare the final combinations.
missions.finish: Both drafted snack halves have been tasted.

missions.title: The wrong-explanation experiment
missions.supplies: A reliable explanation of an everyday phenomenon
missions.description: Tell the difference between a plausible story and an explanation with evidence.
steps: Choose a small question such as why mirrors reverse an image or bread rises.
Each suggest an explanation before checking a reliable source.
Verify the key mechanism and design a harmless observation that distinguishes the ideas.
missions.finish: Your final explanation names the evidence that changed or supported your thinking.
missions.apart: Compare your initial explanations before researching together on a call.

missions.title: The thank-you comic
missions.description: Draw a tiny comic celebrating an actual helpful moment.
steps: Choose something your partner did that made life easier.
Tell it as a three-panel superhero story.
Reveal the comic and explain its real-world inspiration.
missions.finish: Your specific thank-you exists as a finished comic.
missions.apart: Send the comic or reveal it on video.

missions.title: The seasonal trading card
missions.description: Make collectible cards for your current season of life.
steps: Each draw a card with a current hobby or favorite thing.
Add a date, tiny illustration, and silly power rating.
Trade cards and explain your chosen detail.
missions.finish: Both seasonal cards are dated and complete.
missions.apart: Exchange clear photos of your cards.

missions.title: The recipe handoff dinner
missions.supplies: Ingredients for a simple meal you each know
missions.description: Cook a familiar dish using your partner's short instructions rather than a video.
steps: Each write a simple recipe suited to what the other already has.
Exchange recipes, clarify missing details, and prepare your versions normally.
Eat together and give the recipe one concrete correction for next time.
missions.finish: Both recipes have been prepared and improved through an actual handoff.

missions.title: The walking comic captions
missions.description: Write captions that turn three views into a comic.
steps: Notice three safe public scenes along a short route.
Write one caption per scene linking a fictional story.
Read the resulting comic in order.
missions.finish: Your three-scene route tells one connected fictional story.
missions.apart: Combine scene descriptions from your separate routes.

missions.title: The five-minute location match
missions.supplies: A camera and one reference composition you own
missions.description: Recreate a composition using completely different objects from your own surroundings.
steps: Choose a reference with three clear shapes and a defined framing.
Each find substitutes and recreate the layout in five minutes.
Compare which visual relationships survived despite different subjects.
