missions.finish: Your original composition has a recognizable second version.
missions.apart: Exchange reference images and recreate each other's framing locally.

missions.title: The sound-before-picture edit
missions.description: Make a short clip whose sound starts before the image explains it.
steps: Record a harmless distinctive sound and a simple matching visual.
Arrange the sound to begin before revealing its source.
Show it to your partner and ask when they identified the source.
missions.finish: Your clip has a tested sound-led reveal.
missions.apart: Exchange finished private clips and compare the reveal timing.

missions.title: The open-sandwich balance test
missions.description: Build an open sandwich that stays balanced through the final bite.
steps: Choose three familiar toppings with different textures.
Make two small versions changing only the order of the layers.
Taste and compare which structure holds together and tastes more balanced.
missions.finish: Your final sandwich has a tested layer order.
missions.apart: Exchange your layer diagrams and compare separate tasting results.

missions.title: The wind-and-leaf field note
missions.supplies: Paper and two plants visible from one comfortable spot
missions.description: Observe whether two different leaf shapes move differently in the same breeze.
steps: Choose two nearby plants without touching or changing them.
Watch three ordinary breezes and sketch their movement patterns.
Compare the patterns and list one factor other than leaf shape that might matter.
missions.finish: Your field note records repeated movement observations and an alternative explanation.
missions.apart: Compare your separate notes and avoid assuming the wind conditions matched.

missions.title: The quiet postcard puzzle
missions.description: Make a cozy drawing with five tiny hidden objects.
steps: Draw a simple room or garden scene.
Hide five clearly drawn objects within the picture.
Trade pictures and reveal the five-object checklist afterward.
missions.finish: Both hidden-object postcards have been solved.
missions.apart: Exchange clear photos for the puzzle hunt.

missions.title: The free-history label hunt
missions.description: Find three verified facts on public information signs.
steps: Choose an accessible route with official information panels.
Read three signs and each nominate one surprising fact.
Draw a three-fact mini tour card.
missions.finish: Your tour card contains three checked local facts.

missions.title: The humming treasure clues
missions.supplies: Your voice and three household objects
missions.description: Link original musical clues to everyday objects.
steps: Choose three objects and invent a short theme for each.
Play or hum the themes in a shuffled order.
Your partner matches them to the object lineup.
missions.finish: All three musical object clues have been matched.
missions.apart: Show your object lineup on video and exchange themes.

missions.title: The paper ball sorting machine
missions.supplies: Cardboard, tape, and two paper-ball sizes
missions.description: Build a manual sorter for two sizes of paper balls.
steps: Make a small tray with a suitably sized opening.
Test which paper balls fall through and which stay.
Adjust the opening and sort a mixed batch.
missions.finish: Your sorter separates a complete mixed batch.

missions.title: The shared pixel-picture puzzle
missions.supplies: Your shared sketchpad or matching five-by-five paper grids
missions.description: Solve a small hidden picture using row and column clues.
steps: Secretly fill squares in a five-by-five grid and list consecutive filled runs in each row and column.
Exchange the run clues without the picture; for example 2,1 means two filled squares, a gap, then one.
Solve the clues and compare pictures, checking any valid alternative rather than forcing one answer.
missions.finish: Both hidden pictures have a clue-matching solution or a demonstrated valid alternative.
missions.apart: Use your shared Hangouts sketchpad for the solving grid while keeping the original private.

missions.title: The afternoon tourist badge
missions.description: Become tourists by visiting two free local landmarks.
steps: Check public access and choose a manageable short route.
Visit both and notice one detail you had missed.
Draw a small badge showing your two discoveries.
missions.finish: Your tourist badge records two actual visited places.

missions.title: The silent movie moment
missions.description: Act out a tiny disaster without saying a word.
steps: Choose a situation such as a runaway sandwich.
Perform it silently for thirty seconds.
Your partner narrates what they think happened.
missions.finish: You have performed and narrated both tiny disasters.
missions.apart: Use video for the silent performances.

missions.title: The illustrated street name
missions.description: Turn nearby street names into a ridiculous illustrated story.
steps: Collect three street names on a familiar public route.
Use their literal meanings as characters or settings.
Sketch a three-panel story that connects them.
missions.finish: Your route has become a miniature comic.
missions.apart: Each contribute street names from your area.

missions.title: The secret-picture bookmark
missions.description: Design a bookmark whose hidden picture appears when it is folded.
steps: Draw one picture split across a fold on a paper strip.
Add a different visible design when the strip lies flat.
Swap bookmarks and find the fold that reveals the secret image.
missions.finish: Both bookmarks display two deliberately different pictures.
missions.apart: Exchange flat photos and ask your partner where to fold.

missions.title: The drawing telephone
missions.description: See how far one picture changes through repeated translation.
steps: Write a strange sentence and hide it after drawing.
Your partner describes the drawing in a new sentence.
Repeat drawing and describing for four exchanges.
missions.finish: Your final picture can be compared with the original.

missions.title: The tiny picnic tray
missions.description: Build a picnic small enough to fit on one tray.
steps: Choose a drink and three small snack portions.
Arrange them with a folded-paper place marker.
Carry the tray to a comfortable spot at home.
missions.finish: Your one-tray picnic has been enjoyed together.

missions.title: The Morse message club
missions.description: Learn enough Morse code to exchange one tiny message.
steps: Look up a reliable Morse alphabet.
Encode a short friendly phrase using dots and dashes.
Trade messages and decode without revealing the phrase.
missions.finish: Both coded phrases have been correctly decoded.
missions.apart: Send the coded messages as text or voice taps.

missions.title: The ready-in-five celebration
missions.description: Create a celebration setup that can be assembled in five minutes.
steps: Choose three reusable pieces for a real upcoming small occasion.
Build a simple setup and pack its parts into one container.
Time a second assembly and improve any awkward step.
missions.finish: Your complete celebration setup can be assembled within five minutes.

missions.title: The song-before-the-story exchange
missions.description: Guess why a real song matters before hearing its personal backstory.
steps: Each choose a song connected to one specific lived moment.
Listen first and let your partner guess its connection.
Tell the actual story and save a short note beside the song title.
missions.finish: Two songs have their specific personal stories recorded.
missions.apart: Use your own accessible copies and exchange the backstories on a call.

missions.title: The remote museum audio guide
missions.description: Create audio tours for each other's chosen artworks.
steps: Each select one publicly viewable museum artwork.
Record a one-minute tour using the museum's verified label.
Swap tours before discussing what you noticed.
missions.finish: Both selected works have a checked mini audio guide.

missions.title: The tiny actual detour
missions.description: Test one overlooked public route and keep only the details worth returning for.
steps: Each nominate a public spot within a comfortable fifteen-minute reach.
Agree a workable route and visit both without adding more stops.
Choose one useful or enjoyable reason to revisit each location.
missions.finish: Two actual visited spots each have a specific reason to return.

missions.title: The three-depth photo challenge
missions.supplies: A camera and three small props
missions.description: Create a photograph with a deliberate foreground, middle, and background.
steps: Choose a scene where you can stand comfortably without blocking anyone.
Place permitted props or choose existing details at three depths.
Reframe until your partner can identify all three intended layers.
missions.finish: Your selected photo contains three clearly intentional depth layers.

missions.title: The director commentary track
missions.supplies: One of your own short clips
missions.description: Record a funny director's commentary for your own everyday video.
steps: Choose a clip everyone shown agrees to use.
Invent grand artistic reasons for its ordinary details.
Record a short commentary while it plays.
missions.finish: Your ordinary clip has its own private director commentary.
missions.apart: Watch and narrate the selected clip on a call.

missions.title: The biscuit tasting counter
missions.description: Style a tiny biscuit tasting bar using pantry favorites.
steps: Choose three familiar toppings that suit both of you.
Decorate small biscuit portions in three styles.
Arrange a café display and choose a favorite.
missions.finish: Your biscuit bar contains three tested topping styles.

missions.title: The three-layer soundscape
missions.description: Map nearby outdoor sounds as three visual layers.
steps: Listen from one safe comfortable stationary spot.
Draw close, middle-distance, and far-away sounds in separate bands.
Give your soundscape an original concert title.
missions.finish: Your three-layer listening map is complete.
missions.apart: Compare sound maps made at the same agreed time.

missions.title: The warm-light still life
missions.supplies: A cool lamp, three objects, and paper
missions.description: Draw a small still life in comfortable evening light.
steps: Arrange three ordinary objects beside a cool lamp.
Each sketch the scene for ten unhurried minutes.
Reveal the sketches and give them gallery titles.
missions.finish: Both evening still-life sketches are finished.
missions.apart: Sketch your own arrangements and exchange images.

missions.title: The secondhand book forecast
missions.supplies: A library or browsing-friendly used bookshop
missions.description: Predict a book's plot before reading its actual blurb.
steps: Each choose a cover without opening the book first.
Invent a three-sentence prediction from the artwork.
Read the blurb and compare your imagined versions.
missions.finish: Both book predictions have been checked against their blurbs.

missions.title: The melody memory delay
missions.supplies: Your voices and a recorder if desired
missions.description: See which details of a short original melody survive a distraction.
steps: One person hums a four-note original phrase twice.
Do a thirty-second unrelated counting task before the other repeats the phrase.
Compare the repeat with the original and switch roles.
missions.finish: Both delayed melody attempts have been compared with their originals.
missions.apart: Send the original phrase, delay task, and repeat through voice notes.

missions.title: The lightweight domino trail
missions.description: Create a tiny falling-card sequence with a designed finale.
steps: Fold scrap cards so they stand lightly.
Arrange a short path on a clear table.
Test gaps until one gentle push completes the sequence.
missions.finish: Your paper-card sequence reaches its planned ending.

missions.title: The online fossil detectives
missions.description: Investigate one fossil through an official free collection page.
steps: Choose a museum object page with a clear label.
Find its name, approximate age, and one visible feature.
Draw a fictional visitor guide clearly separating fact from imagination.
missions.finish: Your fossil guide contains three checked facts or observations.
missions.apart: Explore the same object page remotely.

missions.title: The initials snack challenge
missions.description: Build a shared snack around the first letters of your names.
steps: Find suitable foods beginning with each chosen initial.
Check ingredients and keep within your agreed total.
Combine the chosen foods as a little tasting plate.
missions.finish: Your initials have become an actual shared snack pairing.

missions.title: The sound impostor
missions.description: Recreate an everyday sound using something completely different.
steps: Choose a familiar sound such as footsteps or a zipper.
Make an imitation using only nearby props.
Let your partner guess both the sound and its unlikely source.
missions.finish: Both players have solved one two-part sound mystery.
missions.apart: Send audio clues before showing your sound-making props.

missions.title: The entrance guessing game
missions.description: Guess what a building is used for before checking its public sign.
steps: Choose three public-facing buildings that are unfamiliar to you.
Each privately guess the purpose from visible exterior clues.
Check official public signage and compare the clues you trusted.
missions.finish: Three building-use guesses have been checked against public information.
missions.apart: Exchange public exterior images before revealing their signs.

missions.title: The pop-up landscape
missions.description: Make a folded card with a scene that stands up.
steps: Fold a card and cut two simple pop-up tabs.
Attach paper scenery to the tabs.
Open it together and add one surprise detail.
missions.finish: Your landscape stands when the card opens.

missions.title: The mystery-weight league
missions.description: Rank objects by weight using guesses before testing.
steps: Choose five manageable objects without fragile contents.
Each write a predicted lightest-to-heaviest order.
Compare by hand or kitchen scale and score matches.
missions.finish: Both predictions have been tested against the final order.

missions.title: The spice aroma atlas
missions.description: Map familiar cooking aromas without turning it into a taste test.
steps: Select three spices you normally use for cooking.
Gently smell each at a comfortable distance.
Describe each as a place and draw the aroma map.
missions.finish: Your map contains three named aroma destinations.
missions.apart: Compare aroma maps using your own familiar spices.

missions.title: The local word detectives
missions.description: Investigate where one wonderfully odd word came from.
steps: Each nominate an unfamiliar word you have encountered.
Check its meaning and origin in a reliable dictionary.
Use both words in a tiny invented news report.
missions.finish: Your report correctly uses two newly learned words.
missions.apart: Perform your joint news report on a call.

missions.title: The beginner-proof walkthrough
missions.supplies: Paper and one useful skill you know
missions.description: Teach a practical skill without skipping the step experts take for granted.
steps: Choose a skill your partner genuinely wants to try.
Give only the instructions needed for a first successful attempt.
Let them try without interruption and improve the missing instruction afterward.
missions.finish: Your partner completes the task using the revised short walkthrough.
missions.apart: Test your instructions over video using suitable materials.

missions.title: The tiny illustrated timeline
missions.description: Tell a shared outing as six tiny pictures.
steps: Choose one outing you both remember.
Draw six moments without worrying about realism.
Compare timelines and add one forgotten detail.
missions.finish: Your outing has a complete six-picture timeline.
missions.apart: Exchange timelines before discussing the differences.

missions.title: The two-house escape signal
missions.description: Exchange a code whose two halves live in different rooms.
steps: Each invent three picture symbols with clear meanings.
Share keys and encode a tiny fictional rescue message.
Decode both halves to reveal the full phrase.
missions.finish: Your two-part message has been decoded.

missions.title: The neighborhood materials match
missions.description: Find the same material doing three completely different jobs.
steps: Choose a common visible material such as wood or metal.
Find three public-facing examples with distinct purposes.
Compare why the material works differently in each example.
missions.finish: Your three finds show one material solving three real design needs.
missions.apart: Exchange examples from your separate neighborhoods.

missions.title: The ordinary-object closeup quiz
missions.supplies: A camera and five household objects
missions.description: Make five close-up puzzles from very ordinary objects.
steps: Take tightly cropped photos without hiding unsafe objects.
Give your partner three guesses per image.
Reveal the full-object photos and compare surprises.
missions.finish: All five close-up mysteries have been revealed.
missions.apart: Send cropped images followed by the full reveals.

missions.title: The three-line scene roulette
missions.description: Improvise a scene around three randomly drawn lines.
steps: Each write three harmless dramatic sentences.
Draw three and use them in order.
End the scene immediately after the third line.
missions.finish: Your improvised scene successfully includes all three prompts.
missions.apart: Send lines privately and perform the scene on a call.

missions.title: The recipe without the numbers
missions.supplies: A familiar no-cook recipe and its normal ingredients
missions.description: See which measurements you actually know before checking your usual recipe.
steps: Choose a suitable familiar no-cook snack.
Write your predicted ingredient ratios before checking the recipe.
Prepare the normal checked version and compare it with your predictions.
missions.finish: Your recipe knowledge has been checked against a real prepared snack.
missions.apart: Choose separate familiar snacks and compare the most surprising ratio.

missions.title: The tree you can find again
missions.supplies: Paper and a familiar public path
missions.description: Learn enough real identifying details to recognize one tree without its location cue.
steps: Observe one accessible tree's leaves, bark, and overall shape without damaging it.
Draw three distinctive details and check a reputable identification guide if useful.
Have your partner identify your selected tree from the details among nearby options.
missions.finish: Your tree can be matched using three observed features.
missions.apart: Use three suitable public tree images and exchange detail clues.

missions.title: The future-guest room test
missions.supplies: Paper and the space you normally use
missions.description: Check whether your imaginary welcome instructions make sense to an actual guest.
steps: One person writes a short guide to three ordinary room features.
The other follows it literally, asking questions only when the guide fails.
Revise unclear steps and add one kind detail a guest would appreciate.
missions.finish: Your three-feature room guide has been tested by another person.

missions.title: The public-space seat study
missions.supplies: Paper and a comfortable public place
missions.description: Find which public sitting spot works best for two different real purposes.
steps: Choose purposes such as quiet reading and watching an open view.
Test three available seats without occupying anything in use.
Score only the features relevant to your two purposes.
missions.finish: Your comparison identifies a different best seat for each purpose.

missions.title: The rhythm code message
missions.supplies: Paper and a soft tapping surface
missions.description: Encode a tiny phrase using agreed rhythmic symbols.
steps: Assign simple tap patterns to four short words.
Make a three-word message using the patterns.
Tap it for your partner to decode.
missions.finish: Both rhythmic messages have been correctly decoded.
missions.apart: Send gentle tap recordings with the same code key.

missions.title: The recycled mascot stand
missions.description: Build a freestanding mascot for your imaginary club.
steps: Draw a character and a simple base shape.
Cut or fold a support so it stands.
Give the mascot a name and welcome speech.
missions.finish: Your original mascot stands and has introduced itself.
missions.apart: Reveal mascot stands and exchange welcome speeches on video.

missions.title: The free city-camera postcard
missions.description: Observe a distant public view without leaving home.
steps: Choose a clearly public scenic camera, avoiding identifiable people.
Look for three landscape or weather details.
Draw a postcard of the view with its actual location.
missions.finish: Your distant-view postcard contains three observed details.
missions.apart: Watch the same public scene on a call.

missions.title: The nearest free performance
missions.description: Try a free public performance you would usually pass over.
steps: Check official times, access, and any free booking requirement.
Choose an event that fits your comfort and schedule.
Attend a suitable portion and compare one detail each noticed.
missions.finish: You have actually experienced and discussed one free performance.

missions.title: The missing ingredient sketch
missions.description: Draw a recognizable object while leaving out its most important part.
steps: Secretly choose an object and omit its defining feature.
Show the drawing and allow three guesses.
Your partner adds the missing part to complete it.
missions.finish: Both incomplete drawings have been guessed and finished.
missions.apart: Send drawing photos to annotate before the reveal.

missions.title: The seven-object route
missions.description: Make a route memorable using seven landmarks, then reproduce it from memory.
steps: Walk one short public route and choose seven distinct landmarks.
Hide the list and sketch their order from memory.
Walk back or check the map to correct your sequence.
missions.finish: Your seven-landmark route has a checked memory version.
missions.apart: Exchange routes drawn on the same free public map.

missions.title: The six-piece tangram dare
missions.description: Cut six shapes and challenge your partner to make three recognizable silhouettes.
steps: Each cut six simple pieces from one square of paper.
Trade a piece set and build an animal, vehicle, and building using every piece.
Photograph each solution before moving the pieces.
missions.finish: Both sets produce three complete six-piece silhouettes.
missions.apart: Use matching paper pieces or a shared simple drawing canvas.

missions.title: The unreliable rule referee
missions.description: Play a tiny grid game where each player must discover one hidden rule.
steps: Draw a shared four-by-four grid with a goal square.
Each choose a hidden movement restriction the other can infer.
Take turns proposing moves and learning from allowed or rejected attempts.
missions.finish: Both players reach the goal and correctly state the hidden rule.
missions.apart: Play on matching paper grids while announcing coordinates.

missions.title: The three-sauce consistency test
missions.supplies: A familiar sauce and suitable normal ingredients
missions.description: Adjust one familiar sauce into three useful consistencies.
steps: Divide a suitable sauce into three small portions.
Use familiar recipe-compatible additions to make a dip, dressing, and drizzle.
Test each on the same food and record the useful ratios.
missions.finish: Your three labeled sauce versions have tested uses and ratios.

missions.title: The origami tutor swap
missions.description: Learn two different folds and teach them from memory.
steps: Each learn a simple model such as a boat or box.
Teach your partner with their own sheet of paper.
Check both models and add a tiny decoration.
missions.finish: Both people have completed both paper models.
missions.apart: Teach the folds close-up over video.

missions.title: The tiny swap shop
missions.supplies: Books or supplies you both own
missions.description: Host a two-person swap shop with playful item descriptions.
steps: Each choose three items you are happy to lend.
Write honest, amusing display labels.
Trade one item and agree when to return it.
missions.finish: Your swap shop has completed one agreed loan each.

missions.title: The unopened prediction split
missions.supplies: Two envelopes or private saved notes
missions.description: Create predictions specific enough to check rather than vague future wishes.
steps: Choose a modest shared event or plan already on your calendar.
Each predict three observable details and write why you expect them.
Seal or privately save the predictions for after the event.
missions.finish: Your future check has six dated, testable predictions.
missions.apart: Keep separate sealed notes with the same reopening date.

missions.title: The tiny remote game show
missions.description: Run a three-round game show from your separate rooms.
steps: Each prepare one drawing, guessing, and quick-thinking challenge.
Take turns hosting the rounds with a shared scoring rule.
Finish with an exaggerated champion interview.
missions.finish: Your game show has completed all three rounds.

missions.title: The clockless minute wager
missions.supplies: A timer and a comfortable sitting place
missions.description: Find out how differently you sense one minute passing in different surroundings.
steps: One person times while the other silently estimates sixty seconds.
Repeat in a second comfortable public setting with roles swapped.
Compare actual durations without checking clocks during either attempt.
missions.finish: Both estimates have a measured result and a compared setting.

missions.title: The one-light portrait lab
missions.supplies: A cool lamp and a camera
missions.description: Explore three portrait moods with one light source.
steps: Choose a comfortable seated pose.
Move the cool lamp to three safe positions.
Select the most interesting portrait and explain the effect.
missions.finish: Your one-light session has three compared portrait moods.

missions.title: The tiny monster sound lab
missions.description: Create a sound identity for an imaginary friendly monster.
steps: Invent the monster's size and favorite activity.
Make a quiet voice, footstep, and happy sound.
Record its three-sound introduction.
missions.finish: Your friendly monster has a complete sound profile.
missions.apart: Swap monster recordings and sketch what you imagine.

missions.title: The savory sundae bowl
missions.description: Present a savory snack in the style of an ice-cream sundae.
steps: Choose normal savory ingredients that work together.
Layer small portions in bowls with an edible garnish.
Reveal the joke and choose the best texture combination.
missions.finish: Your savory sundaes have been assembled and tasted.

missions.title: The daylight palette log
missions.supplies: Paper and colored pens or a camera
missions.description: Capture the colors of one view as the light changes.
steps: Choose a safe fixed view from a window or bench.
Record its three main colors twice fifteen minutes apart.
Compare what actually changed and label both palettes.
missions.finish: Your view has two timed color records.
missions.apart: Trade your paired palettes from different locations.

missions.title: The comfort-snack opening night
missions.description: Host an opening night for a tiny living-room snack bar.
steps: Choose two easy snacks already at home.
Create a menu and an imaginary opening-night invitation.
Serve the snacks with a playful host introduction.
missions.finish: Your two-item snack bar has officially opened.

missions.title: The tiny souvenir budget
missions.description: Choose one modest object as a souvenir of an ordinary outing.
steps: Agree the maximum spend before browsing.
Choose one useful or enjoyable item together.
Write a dated museum-style label for its ordinary-day story.
missions.finish: Your small souvenir has a recorded outing story.

missions.title: The three-track transition draft
missions.description: Build a three-track sequence whose changes feel intentional rather than random.
steps: Choose an opening track for a stated mood.
Take turns choosing the next track based on tempo, texture, or energy.
Listen to the transitions and explain why each handoff works or jars.
missions.finish: Your three-track sequence has two tested and explained transitions.
missions.apart: Use your own accessible copies and compare transition points on a call.

missions.title: The foldable tiny stage
missions.description: Build a stage that folds away after a miniature show.
steps: Fold a backdrop and two side panels.
Add slots for two small paper characters.
Perform a one-minute scene then fold the stage flat.
missions.finish: Your tiny theater has performed and packed away.

missions.title: The digital pattern exchange
missions.supplies: A free drawing tool or squared paper
missions.description: Build an original pattern through alternating rows.
steps: Agree three colors and a small square grid.
Send your first row for your partner to extend.
Alternate until your shared pattern has eight rows.
missions.finish: Your eight-row pattern is complete and jointly made.

missions.title: The sport-from-scratch lab
missions.supplies: A soft ball or rolled socks and paper lines
missions.description: Invent a gentle physical game and actually playtest it.
steps: Choose a clear area and three simple scoring rules.
Play a short first round with comfortable movements.
Change one confusing rule and play a second round.
missions.finish: Your original game has completed two tested rounds.

missions.title: The four-frame flip
missions.description: Make a tiny animation with just four drawings.
steps: Draw an object changing across four frames.
Stack the scraps and flip through them.
Swap animations and add a silly sound effect.
missions.finish: Both four-frame stories can be played.
missions.apart: Send four photos as a quick slideshow.

missions.title: The mini skyline study
missions.description: Draw your local skyline using only rectangles.
steps: Find a safe public viewpoint and sit or stand still.
Sketch its silhouette using ten rectangles or fewer.
Swap drawings and identify the recognizable landmark.
missions.finish: Both skylines can be matched to their view.
missions.apart: Exchange drawings before revealing the original view.

missions.title: The paper roller coaster
missions.supplies: Paper, tape, and a small ball
missions.description: Build a gentle tabletop track with one surprising turn.
steps: Fold paper strips into a low-sided track.
Support a short slope with books.
Test a small ball and improve the turn together.
missions.finish: Your ball completes one full track run.

missions.title: The pencil maze race
missions.description: Design and test mazes with one silly special rule.
steps: Each draw a small maze with three dead ends.
Add a rule such as visiting a star first.
Trade mazes and time a careful solving attempt.
missions.finish: Both rule-based mazes have been solved.
missions.apart: Send maze photos to trace digitally.

missions.title: The toast rescue kitchen
missions.description: Develop a snack that makes stale but still safe bread worth using.
steps: Check the bread is suitable and choose a normal toast or crumb method.
Make two small versions with different familiar toppings or seasonings.
Taste and write down the version you would deliberately make again.
missions.finish: Your bread rescue has produced a repeatable snack recipe.

missions.title: The sound-wave doodle
missions.supplies: A voice recorder with a waveform
missions.description: Discover how different gentle sounds look as waveforms.
steps: Record a hum, soft clap, and spoken word.
Compare their shapes in your recorder's display.
Sketch one waveform as a little landscape.
missions.finish: Your sound landscape comes from an identified recording.
missions.apart: Send waveform screenshots without sharing private speech.

missions.title: The repair lesson swap
missions.supplies: A suitable everyday object and its care instructions
missions.description: Learn one simple maker-approved fix and teach the important step.
steps: Choose a safe task such as sewing a button or tightening a nonpowered fitting.
Use reliable instructions and practice the essential technique together.
Demonstrate the result and note when professional help would be needed instead.
missions.finish: Both people can explain and demonstrate the chosen basic repair.
missions.apart: Teach using matching practice materials on video.

missions.title: The receipt archaeology project
missions.supplies: An old receipt, ticket, or safely shareable digital record
missions.description: Reconstruct a forgotten ordinary outing using one surviving clue.
steps: Choose a record you both agree is suitable to revisit.
Independently reconstruct where you went and what happened around it.
Check the record, keep both accounts, and mark what remains uncertain.
missions.finish: One overlooked record now has a reconstructed, honestly labeled story.

missions.title: The simultaneous skill checkpoint
missions.supplies: A shared free tutorial and suitable materials
missions.description: Learn the same beginner skill, then pause to teach each other the hardest step.
steps: Choose a short free lesson you can both try with available materials.
Attempt it independently before showing your work.
Exchange one practical correction and try again.
missions.finish: Both people have a first attempt and a visibly revised second attempt.

missions.title: The same-shape relay walk
missions.description: Find five different objects sharing one chosen shape.
steps: Choose a shape before leaving on a familiar route.
Collect five public-facing examples without moving them.
Arrange your finds from smallest-looking to largest-looking.
missions.finish: Your five-object shape family is complete.
missions.apart: Each collect part of the same shape family.

missions.title: The photo you can describe
missions.description: Make a photograph your partner can reconstruct from a precise spoken description.
steps: Each take a simple image of objects or a public detail.
Describe its framing, main shapes, and light without showing it.
Your partner sketches the description, then compares it with the photo.
missions.finish: Both photographs have a reconstructed composition and a checked description.
missions.apart: Exchange descriptions by voice note before revealing the images.

missions.title: The split-screen matching action
missions.description: Create matching clips where an action passes between your rooms.
steps: Agree a direction and a small prop type.
Film one person sending and the other receiving off-frame.
Play the clips in sequence to complete the illusion.
missions.finish: Your paired clips suggest one action across two places.

missions.title: The two-tone pancake studio
missions.supplies: A familiar pancake recipe and topping
missions.description: Make a simple two-tone design on a familiar breakfast.
steps: Use a pancake method you already know.
Add a familiar contrasting topping in a deliberate pattern.
Compare designs and enjoy your breakfast together.
missions.finish: Your breakfast plates each have an original two-tone design.

missions.title: The flower geometry notebook
missions.description: Observe flower shapes as a little geometry challenge.
steps: Look closely without picking or touching flowers.
Sketch three visible arrangements of petals or leaves.
Invent a tile pattern inspired by one arrangement.
missions.finish: Your original tile design comes from an observed plant form.
missions.apart: Exchange sketches and compare your pattern designs.

missions.title: The tiny blanket puppet stage
missions.description: Create a low, comfortable stage for a gentle puppet comedy.
steps: Drape a blanket securely over a low table.
Make two paper characters with contrasting personalities.
Perform a three-minute story with a happy resolution.
missions.finish: Your blanket theater has completed its first show.

missions.title: The library illustration relay
missions.supplies: A public library and your own paper
missions.description: Use a book illustration as a starting point for an original drawing.
steps: Choose a library book with an interesting illustration.
Notice three general visual ideas rather than copying the image.
Draw a new scene inspired by those ideas.
missions.finish: Your library visit has produced an original inspired sketch.

missions.title: The household sound alphabet
missions.description: Build a four-letter alphabet made from gentle sounds.
steps: Assign one distinct sound to each chosen letter.
Write a short fictional word using only those letters.
Perform and decode each other's sound words.
missions.finish: Both sound-alphabet messages have been decoded.

missions.title: The three-move terrarium makeover
missions.supplies: Three decorations already in your shared terrarium
missions.description: Improve one view of your terrarium with exactly three agreed placement changes.
steps: Each suggest one visual problem such as a hidden decoration or crowded foreground.
Agree three changes using only items already owned.
Take turns making the changes and compare the view before and after.
missions.finish: Your shared terrarium has three intentional edits with reasons both people can explain.
missions.apart: Take turns editing your shared world while discussing the same view.

missions.title: The map-distance guess
missions.description: Compare your distance guesses for three well-known public landmarks.
steps: Choose three pairs of publicly identified landmarks.
Each estimate straight-line distances without searching first.
Check using the same map tool and compare the surprises.
missions.finish: Your six distance guesses have been checked consistently.
missions.apart: Send guesses before revealing map measurements.

missions.title: The secondhand stylist challenge
missions.supplies: A modest shared budget and a browsing-friendly shop
missions.description: Style one small secondhand outfit detail for each other.
steps: Agree the budget, comfort limits, and practical item category.
Each nominate one suitable item following the shop's rules.
Choose together whether to buy a favorite within the cap.
missions.finish: Both people have tried or reviewed a partner-styled look.

missions.title: The last five words
missions.description: Start a story your partner must finish with five preselected words.
steps: Give your partner five unrelated ordinary words.
Tell a thirty-second opening with a clear problem.
They have thirty seconds to finish using all five words.
missions.finish: Your joint story ends with all five required words used.
missions.apart: Play by call or exchange two short voice notes.

missions.title: The ten-minute local reset
missions.supplies: A timer and a nearby public place
missions.description: Test a short break you could actually repeat on a crowded day.
steps: Agree an accessible spot ten minutes from your normal routine.
Try the complete trip with a five-minute seated pause.
Choose the one detail that makes the break worth repeating.
missions.finish: You have a timed, tested local break with a workable return route.

missions.title: The pocket-sized marble run
missions.supplies: A small box, paper strips, and a paper ball
missions.description: Build a compact ball run that includes a turn, bridge, and finish cup.
steps: Agree the entire course must fit inside one open box.
Build paper features and test each separately.
Connect them and complete three successful runs.
missions.finish: Your box-sized course works three times without being rebuilt.

missions.title: The slow-motion obstacle replay
missions.supplies: Three comfortable floor markers and a timer
missions.description: Design a gentle movement sequence, then reproduce it at half speed.
steps: Choose three safe movements you can both do seated or standing.
Perform a ten-second sequence while your partner memorizes it.
They reproduce it in twenty seconds without adding or skipping a move.
missions.finish: Both ten-second sequences have a successful half-speed replay.
missions.apart: Show the sequence on video and compare the slow replay.

missions.title: The recipe comic strip
missions.supplies: Paper and a favorite simple recipe
missions.description: Explain a favorite snack entirely through drawings.
steps: Choose a snack with four straightforward steps.
Draw one panel for each step without written instructions.
Ask your partner to explain the recipe from the comic.
missions.finish: Your four-panel recipe can be understood.
missions.apart: Exchange comic photos and decode each other's recipe.

missions.title: The public-domain art rabbit hole
missions.description: Explore one artwork through details before reading its label.
steps: Choose a freely viewable museum collection image.
Each notice three details before reading the description.
Compare observations with one verified fact from the label.
missions.finish: Your artwork has six observations and one checked fact.
missions.apart: Browse the same collection image during a call.

missions.title: The evidence-based encouragement note
missions.description: Turn a recent small achievement into encouragement your partner can believe.
steps: Choose a specific effort you actually witnessed.
Write what they did, what it showed, and one thing that changed because of it.
Read the notes and let each person correct any assumption.
missions.finish: Both people have a specific, accurate encouragement note to keep.
missions.apart: Send or read the notes privately on a call.

missions.title: The tiny blooper reel
missions.supplies: A camera and your own clips
missions.description: Make a kind, private blooper reel from willing footage.
steps: Choose three clips both of you are happy to revisit.
Arrange them with short, affectionate title cards.
Watch together and save only with both people's agreement.
missions.finish: Your three-clip private blooper reel is assembled.
missions.apart: Choose and watch the clips in a shared call.

missions.title: The opposite-city evidence hunt
missions.description: Find proof of the same three everyday ideas in two different places.
steps: Choose three prompts such as repaired, out of place, and unexpectedly useful.
Each find examples in your own space or a comfortable public route.
Exchange evidence and defend which example best fits each prompt.
missions.finish: Your two locations supply six explained matches to three shared prompts.

missions.title: The directions stress test
missions.supplies: Paper and a simple public route
missions.description: Write directions a first-time visitor could follow without asking you questions.
steps: Choose a short safe public route with three unambiguous landmarks.
Write instructions, then have your partner trace them literally on a map.
Fix one assumption or missing turn revealed by the test.
missions.finish: Your short route has a corrected beginner-readable set of directions.
missions.apart: Use a freely viewable public map for the trace test.

missions.title: The visual rhyme hunt
missions.description: Find two different scenes that look unexpectedly related.
steps: Photograph one interesting detail in your own space.
Find another subject matching its pattern or arrangement.
Show the pair and explain the visual rhyme.
missions.finish: Your two subjects form a clear visual rhyme.
missions.apart: Send a first photo for your partner to visually answer.

missions.title: The before-and-after mini film
missions.supplies: A camera and a small creative project
missions.description: Document a real transformation with three useful shots.
steps: Choose a small drawing, folded object, or simple safe craft you can finish.
Record the starting state, one important change, and the finished result.
Edit the three shots into a clip that explains the transformation without narration.
missions.finish: Your three-shot film clearly shows one completed real change.
missions.apart: Exchange clips and identify the important step in each other's process.

missions.title: The salad that travels
missions.supplies: Suitable familiar salad ingredients and two small containers
missions.description: Test how to pack a snack salad that stays crisp for a short trip.
steps: Choose clean suitable ingredients you normally eat.
Pack two small portions with different layer or dressing placement.
Leave them for the same short period under suitable storage and compare.
missions.finish: Your two packing methods have an actual crispness comparison.

missions.title: The tiny explorer field badge
missions.description: Earn an imaginary badge by finding four natural details.
steps: Choose a leaf shape, texture, bird sound, and shadow.
Find examples along a short comfortable public route.
Draw a badge showing all four observed details.
missions.finish: Your four-detail nature badge is complete.

missions.title: The private audio mystery night
missions.supplies: A legally free short audio mystery both can access
missions.description: Solve a short audio mystery together using only clues you actually hear.
steps: Choose an accessible short mystery and agree one pause before its ending.
Each write a suspect or explanation with two audible clues.
Finish listening and compare which clues were fair or misleading.
missions.finish: Your two supported predictions have been checked against the ending.
missions.apart: Listen to your own copies at agreed checkpoints on a call.

missions.title: The two-stop perspective outing
missions.description: See one familiar public landmark from two easy viewpoints.
steps: Choose two accessible spots on a checked short route.
Observe the same landmark from each.
Compare which view makes it feel most unusual.
missions.finish: Your outing has two deliberately compared perspectives.

missions.title: The three-tempo character walk
missions.description: Act the same fictional character at three gentle tempos.
steps: Choose a character with a harmless imaginary errand.
Perform comfortable seated or standing gestures slowly, normally, and briskly.
Compare which tempo makes the character funniest.
missions.finish: Your character has three complete tempo interpretations.
missions.apart: Take turns performing through video.

missions.title: The sock basketball court
missions.supplies: A basket, paper lines, and rolled socks
missions.description: Build and play a miniature soft-ball shooting game.
steps: Place a basket on the floor in a clear area.
Mark three comfortable throwing positions with paper.
Play five shots each and choose one bonus rule.
missions.finish: Your homemade court has a completed first game.

missions.title: The virtual garden sketchbook
missions.description: Discover plant forms through a public online collection.
steps: Choose three clearly labeled plants from an official collection.
Sketch a distinctive shape from each.
Combine the forms into one clearly fictional fantasy plant.
missions.finish: Your original fantasy plant has three documented inspirations.
missions.apart: Trade collection links and final plant sketches.

missions.title: The rapid costume department
missions.description: Create a character using only three safe accessories.
steps: Each select three comfortable things to wear or hold.
Assemble your character without explaining it.
Walk in and deliver the character's signature line.
missions.finish: Both characters have made their dramatic entrance.

missions.title: The local superlatives hunt
missions.description: Award tiny honors to ordinary neighborhood details.
steps: Choose categories: tiniest, wonkiest, and most dramatic.
Find one public-facing detail for each award.
Present your winners with exaggerated ceremony.
missions.finish: All three neighborhood awards have winners.
missions.apart: Combine discoveries from your separate neighborhoods.

missions.title: The tabletop landscape swap
missions.description: Turn ordinary objects into a miniature fantasy landscape.
steps: Each arrange five objects as scenery.
Swap landscapes and explain what you think they depict.
Add one character and act out its arrival.
missions.finish: Both landscapes have hosted their first scene.

missions.title: The disappearing sentence
missions.description: Keep a story coherent while removing one word each turn.
steps: Write a dramatic twelve-word sentence.
Alternate removing a word while retaining some meaning.
Read every new version in a dramatic voice.
missions.finish: You have reached a final three-word story.
missions.apart: Play in a shared note or by message.

missions.title: The one-pan timing puzzle
missions.description: Coordinate a familiar meal so its different parts finish together.
steps: Choose a normal recipe and list the cooking times before starting.
Work backwards to write a shared order of tasks.
Cook at a comfortable pace and note one timing adjustment for next time.
missions.finish: Your meal is served with a tested preparation timeline.

missions.title: The mini typography walk
missions.description: Discover the personalities of three public signs.
steps: Find three different lettering styles along a public route.
Sketch or photograph a word from each.
Assign each style a voice and read the words accordingly.
missions.finish: Your three sign styles have distinct performed voices.
missions.apart: Send your sign samples and swap voice interpretations.

missions.title: The tape-free gift-wrap trial
missions.supplies: Reusable paper or cloth, string, and a small object
missions.description: Develop reusable gift wrapping that stays secure but opens without tearing.
steps: Choose an ordinary object and clean wrapping materials you already own.
Try a fold-and-tie method without tape or permanent marks.
Open it, rewrap it, and improve the weakest fold or knot.
missions.finish: Your wrapping stays secure and survives two complete opening-and-reuse tests.

missions.title: The memory recipe card
missions.description: Write a recipe for recreating one good ordinary moment.
steps: Choose a moment that felt enjoyable and easy.
List its setting, people, and little ingredients.
Write three playful preparation instructions and illustrate them.
missions.finish: Your moment has a finished illustrated recipe card.
missions.apart: Write the recipe together in a shared note.

missions.title: The two-place puzzle postcard
missions.description: Make a postcard that hides a tiny solvable puzzle.
steps: Draw a scene inspired by your day.
Hide a simple code or three visual clues.
Send the postcard and trade solution attempts.
missions.finish: Both postcards' hidden puzzles have been solved.

missions.title: The street-scene postcard duel
missions.description: Sketch the same kind of street scene in different styles.
steps: Choose a scene type such as a crossing or corner.
One draws realistically while the other makes it fantastical.
Swap postcards and explain one invented detail.
missions.finish: Your paired postcards show two styles of everyday life.
missions.apart: Sketch comparable scenes in your different locations.

missions.title: The light-bounce experiment
missions.supplies: A camera, white paper, and a still object
missions.description: Improve one portrait or object photo using a simple reflected-light change.
steps: Choose a comfortable position near ordinary window light.
Take one shot without and one with white paper bouncing light toward the shadows.
Compare the same framing and keep the version with the detail you intended.
missions.finish: Your photo pair isolates the effect of one simple light reflector.

missions.title: The genre-swap fairy tale
missions.description: Retell one familiar fairy tale in a different film genre.
steps: Choose a story and a contrasting genre.
Plan three key scenes with new genre details.
Perform a two-minute version with an ending.
missions.finish: Your fairy tale has a complete alternate-genre performance.
missions.apart: Split the roles across a call.

missions.title: The sauce handoff challenge
missions.supplies: Ingredients for a familiar simple sauce
missions.description: Teach your partner one sauce using a short voice note they can actually follow.
steps: Choose a suitable simple sauce and state all ingredients and measurements.
Record a sixty-second instruction note with its essential order.
Have your partner prepare it and tell you one instruction to improve.
missions.finish: Your sauce instructions have been tested by another cook.
missions.apart: Exchange sauce notes and prepare separate matching attempts.

missions.title: The squirrel-free wildlife narrator
missions.description: Narrate an ordinary outdoor scene without inventing facts.
steps: Observe for five minutes from one stationary spot.
Describe only visible behavior in a documentary voice.
Add an explicitly fictional closing line for fun.
missions.finish: Your mini narration separates observation from imagination.
missions.apart: Take turns narrating your separate window views.

missions.title: The cooperative word ladder
missions.supplies: Paper and a dictionary if needed
missions.description: Turn one word into another by changing only one letter at a time.
steps: Choose equal-length ordinary words and agree what counts as a valid word.
Alternate proposing one-letter changes while recording the chain.
Check questionable steps and find a shorter valid route if possible.
missions.finish: Your shared word ladder has a fully checked path between the endpoints.
missions.apart: Build the chain in shared notes or alternating messages.

missions.title: The new-to-us free activity trial
missions.supplies: An official listing for a free public activity
missions.description: Try a free activity you both usually overlook and record one real takeaway.
steps: Check official access, timing, and any required free booking.
Choose a manageable beginner-friendly session or public demonstration.
Try an available part and each name one thing you learned firsthand.
missions.finish: Both people participate in or observe one real new activity.

missions.title: The humming landscape duet
missions.description: Create an original duet inspired by an imaginary landscape.
steps: Choose a place such as a floating garden.
One makes a repeating gentle background pattern.
The other adds a short original melody, then swap.
missions.finish: Your imagined landscape has a two-part original duet.
missions.apart: Record separate parts or sing alternating sections on a call.

missions.title: The cardboard tunnel city
missions.supplies: Scrap boxes and a small paper traveler
missions.description: Build a miniature city connected by three tunnels.
steps: Choose three boxes as imaginary city districts.
Make paper routes connecting their openings.
Guide the traveler through all three districts.
missions.finish: Your connected tiny city has hosted a complete journey.

missions.title: The five-link curiosity gallery
missions.supplies: Free official collection or reference pages
missions.description: Curate five genuinely interesting discoveries around one odd theme.
steps: Choose a narrow theme such as tiny instruments or old maps.
Find five relevant freely accessible reliable pages.
Give your gallery a title and one sentence per link.
missions.finish: Your five-link gallery can be explored by your partner.
missions.apart: Exchange galleries and choose a shared favorite discovery.

missions.title: The new-breakfast discovery
missions.description: Try one suitable breakfast option neither of you usually orders.
steps: Check a local menu and agree a spending cap.
Choose an unfamiliar suitable option without exceeding the cap.
Enjoy the meal and choose one detail to remember.
missions.finish: Your ordinary breakfast routine includes one real new discovery.

missions.title: The five-minute paper city
missions.description: Build a tiny drawn city by taking alternating turns.
steps: Draw one building and pass the paper.
Add roads and landmarks for four more turns.
Choose a city name and its strangest local law.
missions.finish: Your city has five landmarks and a name.
missions.apart: Take turns adding to a shared drawing.

missions.title: The map-to-memory walk
missions.description: Test how well you can map a short familiar route.
steps: Walk a simple public loop without racing.
Each draw the route from memory afterward.
Compare maps and add one detail the other missed.
missions.finish: Your two maps combine into a fuller route.

missions.title: The relief-print reveal
missions.supplies: Cardboard scraps, paper, and a pencil
missions.description: Make an original textured print from a hidden arrangement of shapes.
steps: Cut simple cardboard shapes and arrange a raised pattern on your own surface.
Lay paper over it and shade with the side of a pencil to reveal the relief.
Trade patterns and make a second print with one deliberate design change.
missions.finish: Your raised pattern produces two compared original prints.
missions.apart: Show the finished prints before revealing the cardboard pattern underneath.

missions.title: The spoon delivery service
missions.supplies: A spoon, paper ball, and books
missions.description: Deliver a paper parcel through a tabletop obstacle course.
steps: Build a short course with books laid flat.
Carry the parcel on a spoon around the course.
Redesign one obstacle and swap delivery roles.
missions.finish: Both couriers have completed the revised route.

missions.title: The neighborhood snack scout
missions.description: Choose one unfamiliar-looking snack from a local shop.
steps: Agree a spending limit and check ingredients together.
Pick one item neither of you has tried.
Share it and invent a better description than the packaging.
missions.finish: Your snack discovery has a joint tasting review.

missions.title: The household lever lab
missions.supplies: A ruler, eraser, and paper ball
missions.description: Explore a simple lever by moving its support point.
steps: Balance a ruler on an eraser at table height.
Move the support and gently lift a paper ball.
Compare which position makes lifting easiest without launching anything.
missions.finish: Your three support positions have been compared.

missions.title: The first-visit voice guide
missions.supplies: A recorder and official information about a public place
missions.description: Record a guide someone could follow before their first visit.
steps: Choose a public place and verify access details from its official source.
Record ninety seconds covering arrival, one useful feature, and what to check that day.
Ask your partner to identify anything unclear and record a cleaner take.
missions.finish: Your short guide answers arrival, usefulness, and current-check questions.
missions.apart: Trade guides from your different areas and test each other's explanations.

missions.title: The first-attempt archive
missions.supplies: A photo or object from a recent joint attempt
missions.description: Preserve a first try before improvement makes you forget it.
steps: Choose something you recently tried rather than an impressive finished result.
Record what failed, what unexpectedly worked, and the next experiment.
Save a dated image with both people's observations.
missions.finish: Your first attempt has an honest record and a concrete next experiment.
missions.apart: Exchange observations and save them alongside the same image.

missions.title: The distant blanket cinema
missions.supplies: A free short film and comfortable seats
missions.description: Turn a free short film into a tiny two-location premiere.
steps: Pick a legally free short film you can both access.
Create matching paper tickets and start together.
Compare your favorite scene after the credits.
missions.finish: Your shared short-film premiere has reached its credits.

missions.title: The public-art tiny review
missions.description: Review one accessible public artwork in exactly twenty words.
steps: Spend five minutes looking closely from a public spot.
Write separate twenty-word reviews without comparing first.
Read them and create a joint exhibition title.
missions.finish: Your artwork has two twenty-word reviews.
missions.apart: Review public artworks in your separate areas.

missions.title: The photographic treasure map
missions.description: Make a navigable map using only cropped object photos.
steps: Choose three safe spots in your own space.
Photograph clues leading from one spot to the next.
Ask your partner to solve the photo sequence.
missions.finish: Your three-photo route has been successfully interpreted.
missions.apart: Solve from photos instead of physically visiting the spots.

missions.title: The two-person sound-effects booth
missions.supplies: A camera and safe household props
missions.description: Create live sound effects for a silent miniature scene.
steps: One person acts a thirty-second harmless scene.
The other provides gentle improvised effects.
Swap jobs and replay the scene with a new mood.
missions.finish: Both people have acted and supplied a sound track.

missions.title: The one-batter texture split
missions.supplies: Ingredients for a reliable familiar baked snack
missions.description: Compare two textures from one batch by changing one recipe-approved variable.
steps: Choose a reliable recipe with a documented thin or thick shaping option.
Split one batch and prepare both shapes without improvising cooking safety.
Cook as directed and compare the cooled results.
missions.finish: Your single-batch test identifies a preferred texture and shaping method.

missions.title: The terrarium behavior notebook
missions.supplies: A resident in your shared terrarium and private notes
missions.description: Observe your resident's actual behavior instead of guessing what it is doing.
steps: Watch one resident for a minute and record its visible activity and position.
Offer one suitable care interaction, then observe again without promising a change.
Compare what actually changed and what you still cannot infer.
missions.finish: Your shared resident has a before-and-after observation from both people.
missions.apart: Watch the same shared world and compare independent notes on a call.

missions.title: The low-stakes project demo
missions.supplies: Something small you have made or learned
missions.description: Give a short demonstration of a hobby detail your partner has never actually seen.
steps: Each choose a specific small technique, collection detail, or work-in-progress.
Show rather than summarize it for three minutes.
Let your partner try one step or explain the detail back accurately.
missions.finish: Both demonstrations include a checked practical takeaway.
missions.apart: Demonstrate through video and choose a step suitable for remote explanation.

missions.title: The free-view detour
missions.description: Add a tiny scenic pause to an ordinary local trip.
steps: Check one nearby publicly accessible viewpoint on a map.
Take a short comfortable detour during a suitable trip.
Record one detail you would otherwise have missed.
missions.finish: Your ordinary journey includes one deliberate new discovery.

missions.title: The same-tempo style switch
missions.supplies: Your hands, voices, or an instrument you own
missions.description: Make one short original rhythm feel different without changing its speed.
steps: Create an eight-beat pattern both people can repeat.
Change only volume, emphasis, or sound while keeping the beat constant.
Have your partner identify the changed feature without seeing your notes.
missions.finish: Your one rhythm has three compared versions at the same tempo.
missions.apart: Exchange short performances and guess the changed feature.

missions.title: The no-tape phone stand
missions.supplies: Scrap cardboard, a ruler, and suitable craft tools
missions.description: Build a usable tabletop stand with slots and folds rather than tape.
steps: Sketch a low stand sized for your own phone using two interlocking cardboard pieces.
Cut and assemble it, then test stability on a clear table before use.
Revise one support or angle and compare the improved version.
missions.finish: Your revised low stand holds its intended position without tape.
missions.apart: Exchange side-view drawings and test each other's improvement suggestion locally.

missions.title: The pixel-room design trade
missions.supplies: A free drawing tool or squared paper
missions.description: Design tiny rooms using a shared eight-by-eight grid.
steps: Agree three required features and four colors.
Each fill a small grid with an original room layout.
Trade layouts and add one imaginary resident.
missions.finish: Both pixel rooms have their required features and a resident.
missions.apart: Exchange images and draw residents on separate copies.

missions.title: The outdoor sketch picnic
missions.supplies: Paper, pens, and familiar packed snacks
missions.description: Pair a tiny free picnic with a shared sketch challenge.
steps: Choose a comfortable accessible public sitting spot.
Each sketch the same visible detail while enjoying your snacks.
Reveal both drawings and give them a joint exhibition title.
missions.finish: Your picnic ends with two drawings of one shared view.

dateIdeas.title: Kitchen counter café
dateIdeas.description: Make a drink each and spend ten minutes telling each other about something outside your usual routine.

dateIdeas.title: A window table
dateIdeas.description: Sit by a window, together or on a call, and invent stories about the view.

dateIdeas.title: Dessert before dinner
dateIdeas.description: Share a small sweet thing and describe the best part of your day so far.

dateIdeas.title: The breakfast invitation
dateIdeas.description: Choose a simple breakfast for your next free morning and send each other a little invitation.

dateIdeas.title: A pocket picnic
dateIdeas.description: Pack one snack and find a comfortable spot for a short picnic. Indoors counts.

dateIdeas.title: The no-agenda call
dateIdeas.description: Make a ten-minute call with no errands to discuss. Follow whatever interests either of you.

dateIdeas.title: Bookshop wish date
dateIdeas.description: Browse a bookshop or library and choose a book you think the other would enjoy. No purchase needed.

dateIdeas.title: One candle dinner
dateIdeas.description: Make an ordinary meal feel special with one small change to the table.

dateIdeas.title: The sunset appointment
dateIdeas.description: Arrange to watch the sky at roughly the same time and describe your different views.

dateIdeas.title: Your favorite aisle
dateIdeas.description: Visit a shop together and show each other your favorite aisle without buying anything.

dateIdeas.title: Homemade tasting flight
dateIdeas.description: Each choose three small foods already at home and compare your tasting notes.

dateIdeas.title: An imaginary reservation
dateIdeas.description: Design a dream restaurant date, including the menu and location, with no budget to arrange.

dateIdeas.title: The blanket cinema
dateIdeas.description: Make a cozy seat, watch a short film together, and trade one favorite moment afterward.

dateIdeas.title: Ten-minute balcony break
dateIdeas.description: Take a drink outside or to an open window and give each other your full attention.

dateIdeas.title: Lunch note exchange
dateIdeas.description: Write a tiny invitation to share your next lunch break, in person or over a call.

dateIdeas.title: An evening in another city
dateIdeas.description: Pick a city and spend fifteen minutes exploring its streets on a map together.

dateIdeas.title: The album café
